sentences.zh: 堂子祭天坤寧宮祀神令節設供求福祀神奉先殿壽皇殿

translations.literal: Tangzi worship of Heaven; Palace of Earthly Tranquility worship of spirits; festival offerings; prayer for blessings; spirit worship; Hall of Ancestors; Hall of Imperial Longevity
translations.idiomatic: Worship of Heaven at the Tangzi; spirit worship at the Palace of Earthly Tranquility; festival offerings; prayers for blessings; offerings to the spirits; the Hall of Ancestors; the Hall of Imperial Longevity

sentences.zh: 安佑宮綏成殿附滿洲跳神儀古

translations.literal: Palace of Tranquil Succor; Hall of Lasting Completion; appended: Manchu spirit-dance ritual, ancient
translations.idiomatic: The Palace of Tranquil Succor and the Hall of Lasting Completion; with an appendix on the ancient Manchu spirit-dance ritual

sentences.zh: 堂子祭天清初起自遼瀋，有設桿祭天禮。

translations.literal: Tangzi worship of Heaven: at the beginning of the Qing, it arose from Liaoshen; there was the rite of erecting poles to worship Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Worship of Heaven at the Tangzi: in the early Qing the practice came from Liaodong and Shenyang, where poles were erected for the worship of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 又於靜室總祀社稷諸神祇，名曰堂子。

translations.literal: Moreover, in a quiet chamber they collectively sacrificed to the altars of soil and grain and the various spirits; it was named the Tangzi.
translations.idiomatic: They also worshipped the gods of soil and grain and other deities together in a quiet chamber, which they called the Tangzi.

sentences.zh: 建築城東內治門外，即古明堂會祀群神之義。

translations.literal: The building was constructed outside the Inner Governance Gate on the east of the city; this is the meaning of the ancient Bright Hall, where all spirits were worshipped together.
translations.idiomatic: The hall was built outside the Inner Governance Gate on the east side of the city, in keeping with the ancient idea of the Bright Hall as a place where all the gods were worshipped together.

sentences.zh: 世祖既定鼎燕京，沿國俗，度地長安左門外，仍建堂子。

translations.literal: After the Founding Emperor had established the capital at Yanjing, following national custom he measured out land outside the Left Gate of Eternal Peace and again built a Tangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Shizu Emperor had made Yanjing the capital, he followed national custom, chose a site outside the Left Gate of Eternal Peace, and built a new Tangzi there.

sentences.zh: 正中為饗殿，五楹，南鄉，匯祀群神，上覆黃琉璃。

translations.literal: At the center was the offering hall, five bays, facing south, where all the spirits were worshipped together; above it was covered with yellow glazed tiles.
translations.idiomatic: At the center stood the offering hall, five bays wide and facing south, where all the spirits were worshipped together; its roof was covered with yellow glazed tiles.

sentences.zh: 前為拜天圜殿，北鄉。

translations.literal: In front was the circular hall for worshipping Heaven, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: In front stood the circular hall for worshipping Heaven, facing north.

sentences.zh: 中設神桿石座，稍後，兩翼分設各六行，行各六重，皇子列第一重，次親王、郡王、貝勒、貝子、公，各按行序，均北鄉。

translations.literal: In the center was set a stone pedestal for the spirit pole; slightly to the rear, on both wings were arranged six rows each, each row having six tiers; imperial sons were placed in the first tier, then in order princes of the first rank, princes of the second rank, beile, beizi, and dukes, each according to row order, all facing north.
translations.idiomatic: A stone pedestal for the spirit pole stood in the center; slightly behind it, on both wings, six rows were laid out, each row with six tiers. Imperial sons occupied the first tier, followed in order by princes of the first rank, princes of the second rank, beile, beizi, and dukes, each in his proper row, all facing north.

sentences.zh: 東南為上神殿，三楹，南鄉。

translations.literal: To the southeast was the Upper Spirit Hall, three bays, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast stood the Upper Spirit Hall, three bays wide and facing south.

sentences.zh: 祭禮不一，而以元旦拜天、出征凱旋為重，皆帝所躬祭。

translations.literal: The sacrificial rites were not uniform, but New Year's Day worship of Heaven and worship upon victorious return from campaign were regarded as important; all were personally performed by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial rites varied, but worship of Heaven on New Year's Day and upon a victorious return from campaign were the most important, and the emperor performed all of these in person.

sentences.zh: 其餘月祭、桿祭、浴佛祭、馬祭，則率遣所司。

translations.literal: The remaining monthly sacrifices, pole sacrifices, Buddha-bathing sacrifices, and horse sacrifices were generally entrusted to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: The monthly sacrifices, pole sacrifices, Buddha-bathing sacrifices, and horse sacrifices were generally delegated to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 崇德建元，定制，歲元旦，帝率親王、籓王迄副都統行禮。

translations.literal: When Chongde was established as the reign title, regulations were fixed: on New Year's Day each year, the emperor led princes of the first rank, feudatory princes, down to deputy lieutenant-generals in performing the rite.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongde reign was inaugurated, regulations were fixed so that on New Year's Day each year the emperor would lead princes of the first rank, feudatory princes, and officials down to deputy lieutenant-generals in performing the rite.

sentences.zh: 尋限貝勒止，已復限郡王止，並遣護衛往掛紙帛。

translations.literal: Soon it was limited to stopping at beile; later it was again limited to stopping at princes of the second rank, and bodyguards were dispatched to hang paper and silk offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Soon participation was limited to ranks no lower than beile; later it was limited to princes of the second rank and above, and bodyguards were sent to hang the paper and silk offerings.

sentences.zh: 凡親祭，前期十二月二十六日，內府官赴坤寧宮請朝祭、夕祭神位，安奉神輿，內監舁行。

translations.literal: For all personal sacrifices by the emperor, on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth month beforehand, officials of the Imperial Household went to the Palace of Earthly Tranquility to request the morning-sacrifice and evening-sacrifice spirit tablets, installed them on the spirit palanquin, and eunuchs carried them in procession.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor sacrificed in person, on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth month beforehand officials of the Imperial Household went to the Palace of Earthly Tranquility to fetch the morning- and evening-sacrifice spirit tablets, placed them on the spirit palanquin, and eunuchs bore them in procession.

sentences.zh: 前引御仗八、鐙四，司俎官六人，掌儀司一人，侍衛十人，導至饗殿供奉。

translations.literal: In front were led eight imperial insignia and four stirrups; six meat-offering officials, one master of ceremonies from the Directorate of Ceremonial, and ten bodyguards escorted them to the offering hall for enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: Eight imperial insignia and four stirrups went ahead; six meat-offering officials, one master of ceremonies from the Directorate of Ceremonial, and ten bodyguards escorted the tablets to the offering hall and installed them there.

sentences.zh: 朝夕獻香如儀。

translations.literal: Morning and evening incense was offered according to the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Incense was offered morning and evening according to the prescribed rite.

sentences.zh: 故事，神位所懸紙帛，月終積貯盛以囊，除夕送堂子，與淨紙、神桿等同焚。

translations.literal: By precedent, the paper and silk hung on the spirit tablets, accumulated at month's end and stored in bags, were sent to the Tangzi on New Year's Eve and burned together with pure paper and the spirit poles.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, the paper and silk hung on the spirit tablets were gathered at the end of each month, stored in bags, and on New Year's Eve sent to the Tangzi to be burned together with pure paper and the spirit poles.

sentences.zh: 時內府大臣率長史、護衛掛新紙帛各二十有七。

translations.literal: At that time a minister of the Imperial Household led the chief steward and bodyguards in hanging new paper and silk, twenty-seven of each.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a minister of the Imperial Household led the chief steward and bodyguards in hanging twenty-seven new sheets of paper and silk.

sentences.zh: 昧爽，帝乘輿出宮，陪祀王公等隨行。

translations.literal: At daybreak the emperor rode in the palanquin out of the palace, and the princes and dukes accompanying the sacrifice followed.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the emperor left the palace in his palanquin, accompanied by the princes and dukes who shared in the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 至堂子內門降，入中門，詣圜殿就拜位，南鄉，率群臣行三跪九叩禮。

translations.literal: Arriving at the Tangzi, he descended at the inner gate, entered the central gate, proceeded to the circular hall and took his place for obeisance, facing south, and led the ministers in performing the three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: At the Tangzi he alighted at the inner gate, entered through the central gate, went to the circular hall and took his place for obeisance facing south, then led the ministers in three kneelings and nine prostrations.

sentences.zh: 畢，迴鑾。

translations.literal: When finished, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 翼日，奉神位還宮。

translations.literal: On the following day the spirit tablets were escorted back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the spirit tablets were escorted back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 康熙十一年，詔元旦拜堂子禮宜明備，用鳴贊官。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kangxi, an edict declared that the New Year's Day rite of worship at the Tangzi should be made clear and complete, and chanting masters were employed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Kangxi reign, an edict ordered that the New Year's Day worship at the Tangzi be conducted with full clarity and that chanting masters be employed.

sentences.zh: 明年，罷漢官與祭。

translations.literal: The following year, Han officials were removed from participation in the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Han officials were excluded from the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，諭令皇子隨行禮，內府大臣圜殿進楮帛畢，次進皇太子楮帛。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, an edict ordered imperial sons to follow in performing the rite; after the minister of the Imperial Household had presented paper and silk in the circular hall, the crown prince's paper and silk were presented next.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year an edict required imperial sons to take part in the rite; after the minister of the Imperial Household had presented paper and silk in the circular hall, the crown prince presented his.

sentences.zh: 月祭，歲正月初旬諏吉，餘月朔日。

translations.literal: Monthly sacrifice: in the first ten-day period of the first month of the year an auspicious day was chosen; in the remaining months it was on the first day.
translations.idiomatic: The monthly sacrifice was held on an auspicious day in the first ten-day period of the first month, and on the first day of each month thereafter.

sentences.zh: 司俎二人，就杉柱上掛紙帛數等。

translations.literal: Two meat-offering officials hung paper and silk of prescribed number on the fir posts.
translations.idiomatic: Two meat-offering officials hung the prescribed number of paper and silk offerings on the fir posts.

sentences.zh: 元旦，案陳時食盤一、醴酒盞。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day, on the table were set one plate of seasonal food and one cup of sweet wine.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day one plate of seasonal food and one cup of sweet wine were set on the table.

sentences.zh: 司香上香，內監執三弦、琵琶，坐甬道西，守堂子人持拍板坐其東。

translations.literal: The incense officer offered incense; eunuchs held the three-stringed lute and pipa, sitting west of the corridor; the Tangzi custodians held clappers and sat to the east.
translations.idiomatic: The incense officer offered incense; eunuchs with the three-stringed lute and pipa sat west of the corridor, while the Tangzi custodians with clappers sat to the east.

sentences.zh: 司祝進跪，司香授盞，司祝受之，獻酒。

translations.literal: The prayer officer advanced and knelt; the incense officer handed him the cup; the prayer officer received it and presented the wine.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer advanced and knelt; the incense officer handed him the cup, which he received and used to present the wine.

sentences.zh: 奏神弦，鳴拍板，拊掌應節。

translations.literal: The spirit strings were played, clappers sounded, and palms were clapped in time with the beat.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit strings were played, clappers sounded, and palms were clapped in time with the music.

sentences.zh: 凡六獻，皆讚歌「鄂囉羅」，守堂子人亦歌。

translations.literal: For all six presentations, they chanted the song "Eluola"; the Tangzi custodians also sang.
translations.idiomatic: For all six presentations they chanted the song "Eluola," and the Tangzi custodians sang as well.

sentences.zh: 獻畢，一叩，興，合掌致敬。

translations.literal: When the presentations were finished, they kowtowed once, rose, and joined palms in salutation.
translations.idiomatic: When the presentations were finished, they kowtowed once, rose, and joined their palms in salutation.

sentences.zh: 弦、板止，司祝執神刀進，奏弦、拍板如初。

translations.literal: The strings and clappers ceased; the prayer officer advanced holding the spirit knife, and the strings and clappers were played as at first.
translations.idiomatic: The strings and clappers fell silent; the prayer officer advanced with the spirit knife, and the strings and clappers resumed as before.

sentences.zh: 司祝一叩，興，司俎讚歌「鄂囉羅」，眾和歌。

translations.literal: The prayer officer kowtowed once and rose; the meat-offering official led the chant of "Eluola," and the assembly joined in song.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer kowtowed once and rose; the meat-offering official led the chant of "Eluola," and all joined in.

sentences.zh: 司祝舉神刀誦神歌曰：「上天之子，紐歡台吉，武篤本貝子，某年生小子，某年生小子，今敬祝者，豐於首而仔於肩，衛於後而護於前。

translations.literal: The prayer officer raised the spirit knife and recited the spirit song, saying: "Son of Heaven above, Niuhuan Taigi, Wuduben Beizi, a lad born in such-and-such a year, a lad born in such-and-such a year—now in reverent prayer: abundant at the head and plump at the shoulder, guarding behind and protecting before.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer raised the spirit knife and recited the spirit song: "Son of Heaven above, Niuhuan Taigi, Wuduben Beizi—a lad born in such-and-such a year, a lad born in such-and-such a year—now in reverent prayer: may he be full at the head and sturdy at the shoulder, guarded from behind and protected before.

sentences.zh: 畀以嘉祥兮，齒其兒而發其黃兮，偕老而成雙兮，年其增而歲其長兮，根其固而神其康兮。

translations.literal: Grant auspicious blessings; teeth his young and hair his yellow; grow old together and become a pair; years increase and ages lengthen; roots firm and spirit healthy.
translations.idiomatic: Grant him auspicious blessings; let his children teethe and his hair turn gold; let husband and wife grow old together; let his years and days increase; let his roots be firm and his spirit sound.

sentences.zh: 神兮貺我，神兮佑我，永我年而壽我兮。」

translations.literal: Spirit, bestow upon me; spirit, protect me; prolong my years and extend my life."
translations.idiomatic: O spirit, bestow upon me; O spirit, protect me; prolong my years and grant me long life."

sentences.zh: 凡三禱，如前儀，誦贊者九。

translations.literal: In all there were three prayers, as in the preceding rite, and nine recitations of praise.
translations.idiomatic: There were three prayers in all, following the preceding rite, with nine recitations of praise.

sentences.zh: 司祝跪，一叩，興，誦贊三。

translations.literal: The prayer officer knelt, kowtowed once, rose, and recited praise three times.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer knelt, kowtowed once, rose, and recited praise three times.

sentences.zh: 弦、板止，復跪，一叩，興，合掌退。

translations.literal: The strings and clappers ceased; he knelt again, kowtowed once, rose, joined his palms, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The strings and clappers fell silent; he knelt again, kowtowed once, rose, joined his palms, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 立桿大祭，歲春、秋二季月朔，或二、四、八、十月上旬諏吉行，桿木以松，長三丈，圍徑五寸。

translations.literal: The great pole-raising sacrifice: in spring and autumn, on the first day of the month, or on an auspicious day in the first ten-day period of the second, fourth, eighth, or tenth month it was performed; the pole wood was pine, three zhang long, five cun in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: The great pole-raising sacrifice was held on the first day of the month in spring and autumn, or on an auspicious day in the first ten-day period of the second, fourth, eighth, or tenth month. The pole was of pine, three zhang long and five cun in girth.

sentences.zh: 先一月，所司往延慶州屬采斫，樹梢留枝葉九層，架為桿，齎至堂子。

translations.literal: One month beforehand, the responsible office went to the jurisdiction of Yanqing Prefecture to select and cut timber; nine layers of branches and leaves were left at the treetop, fashioned into a pole, and brought to the Tangzi.
translations.idiomatic: One month beforehand the responsible office went to the jurisdiction of Yanqing Prefecture to select and fell a tree, leaving nine layers of branches and leaves at the top, fashioned it into a pole, and brought it to the Tangzi.

sentences.zh: 前期一日，樹之石座。

translations.literal: One day beforehand, it was erected on the stone pedestal.
translations.idiomatic: The day before the sacrifice it was set up on the stone pedestal.

sentences.zh: 崇德初，定親王、郡王、貝勒祭三桿，貝子、鎮國、輔國公二，鎮國、輔國將軍一。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongde it was fixed that princes of the first rank and princes of the second rank and beile sacrificed at three poles, beizi and dukes of the state-supporting and state-assisting ranks at two, and generals of the state-supporting and state-assisting ranks at one.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongde reign it was fixed that princes of the first and second ranks and beile might sacrifice at three poles, beizi and state-supporting and state-assisting dukes at two, and state-supporting and state-assisting generals at one.

sentences.zh: 月朔大內致祭，初二日後依次祭，凡祭三桿者，定期內祭其一，過旬祭其二。

translations.literal: On the first of the month the inner court performed sacrifice; from the second day onward sacrifices were performed in order; for those who sacrificed at three poles, within the fixed period one was sacrificed to, and after ten days the second.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the month the inner court performed the sacrifice; from the second day onward others sacrificed in turn. Those entitled to three poles sacrificed at one within the allotted period and at the second after ten days.

sentences.zh: 祀日有數家同者，仍按位為等差，違例多祭與爭先越祭並處罰。

translations.literal: When several families shared the same sacrifice day, rank still determined precedence; violating regulations by sacrificing at extra poles, or competing to sacrifice ahead of one's turn, were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: When several families shared the same sacrifice day, rank still determined precedence; extra sacrifices, or competing to sacrifice out of turn, were all punished.

sentences.zh: 後改定大內至入八分公俱祭一桿，將軍不祭。

translations.literal: Later it was changed and fixed that from the inner court down to dukes of the eighth rank all sacrificed at one pole; generals did not sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Later the rule was changed so that from the inner court down to dukes of the eighth rank all sacrificed at a single pole; generals did not sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 屆日，司香豫懸神幔，炕上置漆案，陳碟三。

translations.literal: On the appointed day, the incense officer beforehand hung the spirit curtain; on the kang was placed a lacquered table with three dishes set out.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the incense officer hung the spirit curtain in advance; on the kang stood a lacquered table with three dishes.

sentences.zh: 前置棻案，黃磁碗二。

translations.literal: In front was placed a sandalwood table with two yellow porcelain bowls.
translations.idiomatic: In front stood a sandalwood table bearing two yellow porcelain bowls.

sentences.zh: 圜殿置二棻案，高者陳爐，卑者陳碗，前設采氈。

translations.literal: In the circular hall two sandalwood tables were set; on the higher one an incense burner was displayed, on the lower bowls, and in front colored felt was spread.
translations.idiomatic: In the circular hall two sandalwood tables were set up: an incense burner on the higher one, bowls on the lower, with colored felt spread in front.

sentences.zh: 司俎二人赴坤寧宮請佛亭及菩薩、關帝像，舁至堂子。

translations.literal: Two meat-offering officials went to the Palace of Earthly Tranquility to request the Buddha pavilion and the images of Bodhisattva and Lord Guan, and carried them to the Tangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Two meat-offering officials went to the Palace of Earthly Tranquility to fetch the Buddha pavilion and the images of the Bodhisattva and Lord Guan, and carried them to the Tangzi.

sentences.zh: 安佛亭於座，像懸幔以三繩，系兩殿神桿間。

translations.literal: The Buddha pavilion was installed on its seat; the images were hung with curtains by three ropes tied between the spirit poles of the two halls.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha pavilion was set on its seat; the images were hung behind curtains from three ropes tied between the spirit poles of the two halls.

sentences.zh: 懸黃幡，掛紙帛，圜殿掛帛亦如之。

translations.literal: Yellow banners were hung and paper and silk offerings suspended; in the circular hall silk was hung in the same way.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow banners were hung and paper and silk offerings suspended; the circular hall was draped with silk in the same manner.

sentences.zh: 饗殿北炕案上陳打糕、搓條餑餑盤九，酒盞三，圜殿高案則盤三盞一。

translations.literal: On the table on the north kang of the offering hall were set nine plates of beaten cake and rolled-strip bread, and three wine cups; on the high table of the circular hall, three plates and one cup.
translations.idiomatic: On the table on the north kang of the offering hall stood nine plates of beaten cake and rolled-strip bread and three wine cups; on the high table in the circular hall, three plates and one cup.

sentences.zh: 每獻，司祝挹碗酒注盞，兩殿祭獻歌禱如前儀。

translations.literal: At each presentation the prayer officer ladled wine from the bowl into the cup; in both halls sacrifice, presentation, song, and prayer followed the preceding rite.
translations.idiomatic: At each presentation the prayer officer ladled wine from the bowl into the cup; in both halls the offerings, chants, and prayers followed the same rite as before.

sentences.zh: 祝辭曰：「上天之子，佛及菩薩，大君先師、三軍之師、關聖帝君，某年生小子，某年生小子，今敬祝者，貫九以盈，具八以呈，九期屆滿，立桿禮行。

translations.literal: The prayer text said: "Son of Heaven above, Buddha and Bodhisattva, the great lord's former teacher, master of the three armies, Lord Guan the Sacred Emperor—a lad born in such-and-such a year, a lad born in such-and-such a year—now in reverent prayer: strung nine to fullness, prepared eight to present; the nine periods fulfilled, the pole-raising rite is performed.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer ran: "Son of Heaven above, Buddha and Bodhisattva, the great lord's former teacher, master of the three armies, Lord Guan the Sacred Emperor—a lad born in such-and-such a year, a lad born in such-and-such a year—now in reverent prayer: strung nine to fullness, prepared eight to present; the nine periods fulfilled, the pole-raising rite is performed.

sentences.zh: 爰系索繩，爰備粢盛，以祭於神靈。」

translations.literal: Now ropes are tied, now grain offerings are prepared, to sacrifice to the spirits."
translations.idiomatic: Now the ropes are tied, now the grain offerings are prepared, to sacrifice to the spirits."

sentences.zh: 餘辭同月祭。

translations.literal: The remaining text was the same as for the monthly sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder followed the monthly sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 卒事，司香卷幔、徹像奉入宮。

translations.literal: When finished, the incense officer rolled up the curtain, removed the images, and escorted them back into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished, the incense officer rolled up the curtain, removed the images, and escorted them back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 若帝親祭，殿內敷采席，覆紅氈，甬道布椶薦。

translations.literal: If the emperor sacrificed in person, colored mats were spread in the hall and covered with red felt; on the corridor palm-fiber mats were laid.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sacrificed in person, colored mats covered with red felt were spread in the hall, and palm-fiber mats were laid along the corridor.

sentences.zh: 屆時乘輿出宮，滿大臣隨扈至堂子街，王公跽俟，興，從之。

translations.literal: At the appointed time he rode in the palanquin out of the palace; Manchu ministers followed in attendance to Tangzi Street; princes and dukes knelt in waiting, then rose and followed.
translations.idiomatic: At the appointed time he left the palace in his palanquin; Manchu ministers accompanied him to Tangzi Street; princes and dukes knelt to await him, then rose and followed.

sentences.zh: 帝降輿入中門，詣饗殿前東鄉坐，司祝獻酒，舉神刀，禱祝，奏弦、拍板，拊掌，歌「鄂囉羅。」

translations.literal: The emperor descended from the palanquin and entered the central gate, proceeded to the offering hall and sat facing east before it; the prayer officer presented wine, raised the spirit knife, prayed, the strings and clappers were played, palms clapped, and they sang "Eluola."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor alighted and entered the central gate, went to the offering hall and sat facing east before it; the prayer officer presented wine, raised the spirit knife, and prayed while strings and clappers sounded, palms clapped, and they sang "Eluola."

sentences.zh: 帝入，一跪三叩。

translations.literal: The emperor entered, performed one kneeling and three kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered and performed one kneeling and three kowtows.

sentences.zh: 圜殿同。

translations.literal: The circular hall was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The same was done in the circular hall.

sentences.zh: 畢，升座，賜王公等炕前坐。

translations.literal: When finished, he ascended to his seat and granted princes and dukes to sit before the kang.
translations.idiomatic: When this was finished, he took his seat and granted the princes and dukes places before the kang.

sentences.zh: 尚膳正、司俎官進胙糕，尚茶正獻福酒，帝受胙，分賜各王公。

translations.literal: The chief steward of the imperial kitchen and the meat-offering officials presented sacrificial meat and cake; the chief steward of tea presented blessed wine; the emperor received the sacrificial portion and distributed it to each prince and duke.
translations.idiomatic: The chief steward of the imperial kitchen and the meat-offering officials presented sacrificial meat and cake; the chief steward of tea presented blessed wine; the emperor received the portion and distributed it among the princes and dukes.

sentences.zh: 禮成，還宮。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 遇壇、廟齋期或清明節，再涓吉以祀。

translations.literal: If it fell during the fasting period for altars or temples, or on Qingming, an auspicious day was again chosen for the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: If the day fell during the fasting period for altars or temples, or on Qingming, another auspicious day was chosen for the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 月朔祀東南隅尚錫神亭，即堂子上神殿也。

translations.literal: On the first of the month they sacrificed at the Shangxi Spirit Pavilion in the southeast corner—that is, the Upper Spirit Hall of the Tangzi.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of each month they sacrificed at the Shangxi Spirit Pavilion in the southeast corner—the Upper Spirit Hall of the Tangzi.

sentences.zh: 神曰田苗，神案上盤一、盞一，分陳時食醴酒，司香上香，司俎掛淨紙杉柱上，諸王護衛依次掛之。

translations.literal: The spirit was called Tianmiao; on the spirit table were one plate and one cup, with seasonal food and sweet wine set separately; the incense officer offered incense; the meat-offering official hung pure paper on the fir post, and princes and bodyguards hung it in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit was called Tianmiao. On the spirit table stood one plate and one cup, with seasonal food and sweet wine set out separately. The incense officer offered incense; the meat-offering official hung pure paper on the fir post, and princes and bodyguards hung theirs in turn.

sentences.zh: 內管領一人入，除冠服，解帶，跪叩，祝辭曰：「上天之子，尚錫之神，月巳更矣，建始維新，某年生小子，敬備粢盛兮，潔楮並陳。

translations.literal: One inner steward entered, removed cap and robe, untied his belt, knelt and kowtowed, and the prayer text said: "Son of Heaven above, spirit of Shangxi—the month has already changed, the founding year renewed—a lad born in such-and-such a year reverently prepares grain offerings; pure paper is set forth together.
translations.idiomatic: One inner steward entered, removed his cap and robe, untied his belt, knelt and kowtowed, and prayed: "Son of Heaven above, spirit of Shangxi—the month has turned, the year begun anew—a lad born in such-and-such a year reverently prepares grain offerings and sets forth pure paper.

sentences.zh: 惠我某年生小子，貺以嘉祥兮，畀以康寧。」

translations.literal: Show favor to this lad born in such-and-such a year; bestow auspicious blessings; grant peace and health."
translations.idiomatic: Show favor to this lad born in such-and-such a year; bestow auspicious blessings and grant him peace and health."

sentences.zh: 畢，退。

translations.literal: When finished, he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 或謂祀明副總兵鄧子龍也，以與太祖有舊誼，故附祀之。

translations.literal: Some say it worshipped Ming deputy regional commander Deng Zilong, and because he had old ties with the Taizu, he was worshipped here as an appended sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that the spirit worshipped was the Ming deputy regional commander Deng Zilong, who was given this appended sacrifice because of his old ties with the Taizu.

sentences.zh: 四月八日佛誕，祭祀前期，饗殿懸神幔，選覺羅妻正、副贊祀二人為司祝。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the fourth month, the Buddha's birthday sacrifice: beforehand the offering hall hung the spirit curtain, and two Aisin Gioro wives, principal and assistant ritual sponsors, were chosen as prayer officers.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the fourth month, the Buddha's birthday sacrifice: beforehand the spirit curtain was hung in the offering hall, and two Aisin Gioro wives, principal and assistant ritual sponsors, were chosen as prayer officers.

sentences.zh: 祭日，不祈報，不宰牲，不理刑名。

translations.literal: On the sacrifice day there were no prayers for blessing or retribution, no slaughter of animals, and no handling of criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: On the sacrifice day no prayers for blessing or retribution were offered, no animals were slaughtered, and no criminal cases were heard.

sentences.zh: 屆時赴坤寧宮請佛亭及菩薩、關聖像，司俎內監置椴葉餑餑、釀酒、紅蜜於盒以從，至則陳香鐙，獻糕酒，取紅蜜暨諸王供蜜各少許，注黃磁浴池。

translations.literal: At the appointed time they went to the Palace of Earthly Tranquility to request the Buddha pavilion and the images of Bodhisattva and Lord Guan; meat-offering eunuchs placed linden-leaf bread, fermented wine, and red honey in boxes to accompany them; on arrival incense lamps were set out, cake and wine presented, a little red honey together with a little of the honey offered by each prince was taken and poured into the yellow porcelain bathing basin.
translations.idiomatic: At the appointed time they went to the Palace of Earthly Tranquility to fetch the Buddha pavilion and the images of the Bodhisattva and Lord Guan; meat-offering eunuchs carried boxes of linden-leaf bread, fermented wine, and red honey. On arrival incense lamps were set out and cake and wine presented; a little red honey together with a little of each prince's offering was poured into the yellow porcelain bathing basin.

sentences.zh: 司祝請佛，浴畢，以新棉承座，還奉佛亭，陳椴葉餑餑九盤，酒盞、香碟各三，並諸王所供餑餑、酒。

translations.literal: The prayer officer invited the Buddha; when the bathing was finished, new cotton was used to support the seat, and the Buddha was returned to the pavilion; nine plates of linden-leaf bread were set out, three wine cups and three incense dishes, together with the bread and wine offered by the princes.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer invited the Buddha; when the bathing was finished, new cotton was placed to support the seat and the image was returned to the pavilion. Nine plates of linden-leaf bread were set out, with three wine cups and three incense dishes, together with the bread and wine offered by the princes.

sentences.zh: 圜殿亦如之。

translations.literal: The circular hall was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The same was done in the circular hall.

sentences.zh: 司香上香，司祝獻酒九巡，餘略如月祭、桿祭。

translations.literal: The incense officer offered incense; the prayer officer presented wine in nine rounds; the remainder followed the monthly and pole sacrifices in general.
translations.idiomatic: The incense officer offered incense; the prayer officer presented wine in nine rounds; the remainder followed the monthly and pole sacrifices in general.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，定八旗王、貝勒各一人，依次供獻。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde it was fixed that each banner should have one prince or beile offer sacrifice in turn.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Chongde reign it was fixed that each banner should have one prince or beile offer sacrifice in turn.

sentences.zh: 厥後唯親王、郡王行之。

translations.literal: Thereafter only princes of the first and second ranks performed it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter only princes of the first and second ranks performed this duty.

sentences.zh: 馬祭，歲春、秋季月，為所乘馬祀圜殿。

translations.literal: Horse sacrifice: in spring and autumn, in the monthly period, sacrifice was performed for the horses one rode in the circular hall.
translations.idiomatic: The horse sacrifice was held in spring and autumn to worship the horses one rode, in the circular hall.

sentences.zh: 正日，司俎掛紙帛如常數，陳打糕一盤、醴酒一琖，縛馬鬃、尾綠二十對。

translations.literal: On the proper day the meat-offering official hung paper and silk in the usual number, set out one plate of beaten cake and one cup of sweet wine, and bound twenty pairs of green strips to the horses' manes and tails.
translations.idiomatic: On the proper day the meat-offering official hung the usual number of paper and silk offerings, set out one plate of beaten cake and one cup of sweet wine, and bound twenty pairs of green strips to the horses' manes and tails.

sentences.zh: 司香上香，牧牽十馬，色皆白，立甬道下。

translations.literal: The incense officer offered incense; herdsmen led ten horses, all white in color, standing below the corridor.
translations.idiomatic: The incense officer offered incense; herdsmen led ten white horses to stand below the corridor.

sentences.zh: 司祝六獻酒，奏樂如儀。

translations.literal: The prayer officer presented wine six times; music was played according to the rite.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer presented wine six times while music was played according to the rite.

sentences.zh: 所禱之神同月祭，唯祝辭則易為所乘馬。

translations.literal: The spirits prayed to were the same as for the monthly sacrifice; only the prayer text was changed to concern the horses one rode.
translations.idiomatic: The spirits addressed were the same as for the monthly sacrifice; only the prayer text was changed to concern the horses one rode.

sentences.zh: 「敬祝者，撫脊以起兮，引鬣以興兮，嘶風以奮兮，噓霧以行兮，食草以壯兮，齧艾以騰兮。

translations.literal: "In reverent prayer: stroking the back to rise; drawing the mane to stir; neighing against the wind to exert strength; snorting mist to advance; eating grass to grow strong; biting mugwort to leap.
translations.idiomatic: "In reverent prayer: may they rise when their backs are stroked, stir when their manes are drawn, neigh against the wind and gallop through the mist, grow strong on grass and leap when they bite mugwort.

sentences.zh: 溝穴其弗逾兮，盜賊其無擾兮。

translations.literal: May ditches and holes not be crossed; may thieves and robbers not disturb.
translations.idiomatic: May they not fall into ditches or holes; may thieves and robbers not trouble them.

sentences.zh: 神其貺我，神其佑我。」

translations.literal: Spirit, bestow upon me; spirit, protect me."
translations.idiomatic: O spirit, bestow upon me; O spirit, protect me."

sentences.zh: 禱訖，取條就香爐薰禱，司俎以授牧長，系之馬尾。

translations.literal: When the prayer was finished, strips were taken and fumigated with prayer over the incense burner; the meat-offering official handed them to the chief herdsman, who tied them to the horses' tails.
translations.idiomatic: When the prayer was finished, strips were taken and fumigated with prayer over the incense burner; the meat-offering official handed them to the chief herdsman, who tied them to the horses' tails.

sentences.zh: 是日，馬神室並奉朝祭、夕祭神位，遣內府大臣行禮。

translations.literal: On that day, in the Horse Spirit Chamber the morning-sacrifice and evening-sacrifice spirit tablets were also enshrined, and a minister of the Imperial Household was dispatched to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: On that day the morning- and evening-sacrifice spirit tablets were also enshrined in the Horse Spirit Chamber, and a minister of the Imperial Household was dispatched to perform the rite.

sentences.zh: 朝祭豫懸幔，舁供佛小亭奉炕上，案陳香、酒、食品。

translations.literal: For the morning sacrifice the curtain was hung beforehand; the small Buddha-offering pavilion was carried and placed on the kang; on the table incense, wine, and food were set out.
translations.idiomatic: For the morning sacrifice the curtain was hung in advance; the small Buddha-offering pavilion was carried to the kang; incense, wine, and food were set on the table.

sentences.zh: 司俎進二豕，熟而薦之。

translations.literal: The meat-offering official presented two pigs, cooked them, and offered them.
translations.idiomatic: The meat-offering official presented two pigs, cooked them, and offered them up.

sentences.zh: 司香上香，舉琖授司祝，司祝進跪三獻，歌奏如前。

translations.literal: The incense officer offered incense, raised the cup and handed it to the prayer officer; the prayer officer advanced, knelt, and presented three times; song and music were performed as before.
translations.idiomatic: The incense officer offered incense, raised the cup and handed it to the prayer officer, who advanced, knelt, and presented three times while song and music were performed as before.

sentences.zh: 訖，授盞司香，一叩，興，合掌致敬。

translations.literal: When finished, the cup was handed to the incense officer; he kowtowed once, rose, and joined his palms in salutation.
translations.idiomatic: When the presentations were finished, the cup was handed to the incense officer, who kowtowed once, rose, and joined his palms in salutation.

sentences.zh: 復跪，祝，一叩，興。

translations.literal: He knelt again, prayed, kowtowed once, and rose.
translations.idiomatic: He knelt again, offered prayer, kowtowed once, and rose.

sentences.zh: 取縛馬鬃、尾紅條七十對，就香碟薰禱，授司俎官，轉授上駟院侍衛，分給各廠、院。

translations.literal: Seventy pairs of strips bound to horses' manes and tails in red were taken, fumigated with prayer over the incense tray, handed to the meat-offering official, transferred to bodyguards of the Upper Stud Farm, and distributed to each stable and yard.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy pairs of red strips bound to the horses' manes and tails were taken, fumigated with prayer over the incense tray, handed to the meat-offering official, passed to bodyguards of the Upper Stud Farm, and distributed to each stable and yard.

sentences.zh: 卿、侍衛、廄長入，隨食肉。

translations.literal: Ministers, bodyguards, and stable chiefs entered and partook of the meat.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers, bodyguards, and stable chiefs entered and shared the sacrificial meat.

sentences.zh: 其夕祭儀略如朝祭，候肉熟分陳案上，進跪叩祝同。

translations.literal: That evening's sacrifice followed the morning sacrifice in general outline; when the meat was cooked it was apportioned and set on tables, and advancing, kneeling, kowtowing, and prayer were the same.
translations.idiomatic: The evening sacrifice largely followed the morning rite: when the meat was cooked it was portioned onto tables, and the advancing, kneeling, kowtowing, and prayers were the same.

sentences.zh: 司祝坐杌置夕祭定處，設小案、小腰鈴，別置神鈴。

translations.literal: The prayer officer sat on a stool at the fixed place for the evening sacrifice, set up a small table and small waist bells, and separately placed the spirit bells.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer sat on a stool at the evening sacrifice's fixed station, set out a small table and small waist bells, and placed the spirit bells separately.

sentences.zh: 案東展背鐙布幕，振鈴桿，搖腰鈴，誦神歌，前後所禱所祝之神詳下。

translations.literal: East of the table the back-stirrup cloth curtain was spread; he shook the bell pole and waist bells and recited the spirit song—the spirits prayed to and blessed before and after are detailed below.
translations.idiomatic: East of the table the back-stirrup curtain was spread; he shook the bell pole and waist bells and recited the spirit song—the spirits addressed in prayer and blessing, before and after, are detailed below.

sentences.zh: 背鐙祭，其辭禱同朝祭，祈請者四，禱後跪祝辭、供肉祝辭亦如之。

translations.literal: For the back-stirrup sacrifice the prayer words were the same as for the morning sacrifice; there were four petitions; after prayer the kneeling blessing text and the meat-offering blessing text were likewise the same.
translations.idiomatic: In the back-stirrup sacrifice the prayers matched the morning rite: there were four petitions, and the kneeling blessing and the meat-offering blessing afterward were the same as well.

sentences.zh: 畢，取縛馬鬃、尾青條三十對，仍就香碟薰禱授如初。

translations.literal: When finished, thirty pairs of strips bound to manes and tails in blue-green were taken and, as before, fumigated with prayer over the incense tray and handed on.
translations.idiomatic: When this was finished, thirty pairs of blue-green strips bound to manes and tails were taken and, as before, fumigated with prayer over the incense tray and passed on.

sentences.zh: 翼日，為牧群滋息，復行朝、夕祭如初禮。

translations.literal: On the following day, for the multiplication of the herds, morning and evening sacrifices were again performed as in the original rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day, to bless the herds with increase, morning and evening sacrifices were again performed according to the original rite.

sentences.zh: 唯祝辭易「今為牧群繁息」六字，「溝穴」二句易為「如萌芽之發育兮，如根本之滋榮兮」，餘辭並同。

translations.literal: Only the blessing text changed the six characters to "now for the multiplication of the herds," and the two lines on "ditches and holes" were changed to "like shoots sprouting in growth; like roots flourishing in vigor"; the remaining words were all the same.
translations.idiomatic: Only the blessing text was altered: the six characters became "now for the herds' increase," and the two lines on ditches and holes became "like shoots sprouting in growth; like roots flourishing in vigor"; all other words remained the same.

sentences.zh: 又司香取縛馬鬃、尾條二百八十對，皆青色。

translations.literal: Also the incense officer took two hundred eighty pairs of strips bound to manes and tails, all blue-green.
translations.idiomatic: The incense officer also took two hundred eighty pairs of strips bound to manes and tails, all blue-green.

sentences.zh: 崇德初制，為馬群致祭，唯親王至輔國公得行。

translations.literal: In the initial Chongde regulations, sacrifice was performed for the horse herds; only princes of the first rank down to subsidiary state dukes might perform it.
translations.idiomatic: Under the initial Chongde regulations, sacrifice was offered for the horse herds; only princes of the first rank down to subsidiary state dukes were permitted to perform it.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年，定春、秋騸馬致祭，薩滿叩頭。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong, spring and autumn sacrifices for gelded horses were fixed, with the shaman kowtowing.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year of the Qianlong reign, spring and autumn sacrifices for gelded horses were established, with the shaman performing the kowtow.

sentences.zh: 薩滿者，贊祀也。

translations.literal: The shaman is the one who leads the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The shaman is the one who assists at the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 訖，取所送青色十馬系綠條如數。

translations.literal: When finished, the ten blue-green horses sent were taken and green strips tied in the same number.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished, the ten blue-green horses presented were taken and green strips tied on in the same number.

sentences.zh: 又定朝祭御馬拴紅條，大凌河騾馬拴青條，為恆制。

translations.literal: It was also fixed that for the morning sacrifice imperial horses were tied with red strips, and mules and horses at Daling River with blue-green strips, as a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: It was also decreed that imperial horses at the morning sacrifice should wear red strips, and mules and horses at Daling River blue-green strips, as a standing rule.

sentences.zh: 凡出師凱旋，皆有事堂子。

translations.literal: Whenever troops set out or returned victorious, there were rites at the Tangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the army marched out or returned in victory, rites were performed at the Tangzi.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，太宗征明及朝鮮，明年班師，並告祭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde the Taizong campaigned against the Ming and Korea; the next year, when the army returned, sacrifices of announcement were performed for both.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde the Taizong campaigned against the Ming and Korea; the next year, when the armies returned, announcement sacrifices were performed for both campaigns.

sentences.zh: 世祖定中原，建堂子。

translations.literal: When the Shizu emperor consolidated the Central Plain, he built the Tangzi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizu emperor secured the Central Plain, he built the Tangzi.

sentences.zh: 嗣是聖祖平吳三桂、察哈爾，迄歷朝靖亂，皆以禮祗告。

translations.literal: Thereafter, when the Sage Ancestor suppressed Wu Sangui and the Chahar, and through successive reigns disorder was pacified, all were respectfully announced by rite.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, when the Sage Ancestor put down Wu Sangui and the Chahar, and through successive reigns rebellions were quelled, all were respectfully announced in ritual.

sentences.zh: 凡親征告祭命下，涓吉，屆期兵部建大纛，具祀纛篇。

translations.literal: Whenever an order was issued for sacrifice of announcement on a personal campaign, an auspicious day was chosen; when the day arrived the Board of War erected the great banner and prepared the text for sacrifice to the banner.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an edict ordered the announcement sacrifice for an imperial campaign, an auspicious day was chosen; when the day came the Board of War raised the great banner and prepared the liturgy for the banner sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 帝御戎服，出宮乘騎，前後翊衛，午門鳴鐘鼓，法駕鹵簿為導，饒歌大樂，備而不作。

translations.literal: The emperor donned military dress, left the palace mounted, with bodyguards before and behind; at the Meridian Gate bells and drums sounded; the imperial guard of honor led as escort; the triumphal songs and great music were prepared but not played.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore military dress, left the palace on horseback, with bodyguards before and behind; at the Meridian Gate bells and drums sounded; the imperial guard of honor went ahead as escort; triumphal songs and great music were ready but not performed.

sentences.zh: 至玉河橋，軍士鳴角螺，帝入堂子街門降騎，角螺止。

translations.literal: At Jade River Bridge the soldiers sounded conch horns; the emperor entered the Tangzi street gate and dismounted; the conch horns ceased.
translations.idiomatic: At Jade River Bridge the soldiers sounded conch horns; the emperor entered the Tangzi street gate and dismounted, and the horns fell silent.

sentences.zh: 入中門，詣圜殿就拜位，南鄉立，率群臣行三跪九叩禮。

translations.literal: Entering the central gate, he proceeded to the circular hall and took his place for obeisance, standing facing south, and led the ministers in three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the central gate, went to the circular hall and took his place for obeisance facing south, then led the ministers in three kneelings and nine prostrations.

sentences.zh: 角螺齊鳴。

translations.literal: The conch horns sounded together.
translations.idiomatic: The conch horns sounded in unison.

sentences.zh: 出內門，致禮纛神。

translations.literal: Leaving the inner gate, he performed rites to the banner spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the inner gate, he performed rites to the banner spirit.

sentences.zh: 禮成，樂作，車駕啟行。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, music played and the imperial procession set out.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, music sounded and the imperial procession departed.

sentences.zh: 凱旋日，率大將軍及從征將士詣堂子告成。

translations.literal: On the day of victorious return he led the grand general and the officers and soldiers who had campaigned to the Tangzi to announce completion.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of victorious return he led the grand general and the officers and soldiers who had campaigned to the Tangzi to announce the completed campaign.

sentences.zh: 若命重臣經略軍務以討不庭，禮亦如之。

translations.literal: If a senior minister was ordered to direct military affairs and punish the rebellious, the rite was likewise observed.
translations.idiomatic: If a senior minister was commissioned to direct military affairs and punish those who would not attend court, the rite was observed in the same way.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十四年，詔言：「堂子致祭，所祭即天神也。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong, an edict stated: "Sacrifice at the Tangzi—the objects worshipped are Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong an edict declared: "Sacrifice at the Tangzi is worship of Heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 列祖御宇，稽古郊禋，燔柴鉅典，舉必以時。

translations.literal: Our successive ancestors ruling the realm examined antiquity for suburban and border sacrifices; the great rite of burning firewood was always performed at the proper season.
translations.idiomatic: Our successive emperors, ruling the realm, looked to antiquity for suburban and border sacrifices; the great rite of burning firewood was always performed at its proper season.

sentences.zh: 堂子則舊俗相承，凡遇大事，及春、秋季月上旬，必祭天祈報，歲首尤先展禮。

translations.literal: The Tangzi followed old custom handed down: whenever great matters arose, and in the first ten-day period of spring and autumn, Heaven was necessarily worshipped in prayer and thanksgiving; at year's beginning the rite was especially performed first.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangzi preserved custom handed down from old times: whenever great affairs arose, and in the first ten-day period of spring and autumn, Heaven was worshipped in prayer and thanksgiving; at the year's beginning the rite was especially performed first.

sentences.zh: 定鼎以來，恪遵舊制。

translations.literal: Since the founding of the capital, the old system has been scrupulously followed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the capital was established, the old system has been scrupulously observed.

sentences.zh: 考經訓祭天，有郊、有類，有祈穀、祈年，禮本不一。

translations.literal: Examining the classics and teachings on worship of Heaven, there are suburban rites, border rites, prayers for grain and prayers for harvest—the rites are not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: The classics and teachings on worship of Heaven show suburban rites, border rites, prayers for grain and prayers for harvest—the rites are not one and the same.

sentences.zh: 兵戎國之大事，命將先禮堂子，正類祭遺意，禮纛即禡也。

translations.literal: War is a great matter of state; when appointing generals the Tangzi is worshipped first—this preserves the idea of the border sacrifice; worshipping the banner is worshipping the war god.
translations.idiomatic: War is a great matter of state; when generals are appointed the Tangzi is worshipped first—this preserves the intent of the border sacrifice; worship of the banner is worship of the war god.

sentences.zh: 或在行營別有征討，不及祭告堂子，則行望祭，其誠敬如此。

translations.literal: Or if in camp there were separate campaigns and sacrifice could not be announced at the Tangzi, a sacrifice toward Heaven was performed—such was the reverence and respect.
translations.idiomatic: If in camp there were separate campaigns and announcement at the Tangzi was impossible, a sacrifice toward Heaven was performed instead—such was the reverence shown.

sentences.zh: 夫出師告遣，凱旋即當告至。

translations.literal: When troops set out, announcement and send-off should be made; on victorious return, arrival should immediately be announced.
translations.idiomatic: When troops set out, departure should be announced; on victorious return, arrival should be announced at once.

sentences.zh: 乃天地、宗社皆已祝冊致虔，且受成太學，而堂子則弗及，禮官疏略，如神貺何？

translations.literal: Yet Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temple had all received earnest prayer by written invocation, and success was received at the Imperial Academy—while the Tangzi was not reached; the ritual officers were remiss—how could the spirits bestow blessings?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temple had all received earnest prayer by written invocation, and victory was reported at the Imperial Academy—while the Tangzi was left out; the ritual officers were remiss—how could the spirits grant their blessings?

sentences.zh: 其詳議以聞。」

translations.literal: Let the matter be fully deliberated and reported."
translations.idiomatic: Let the matter be fully deliberated and reported to Us."

sentences.zh: 尋奏凱旋、告祭之禮。

translations.literal: Soon memorials on the rites of victorious return and sacrifice of announcement were submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon thereafter memorials on the rites of victorious return and announcement sacrifice were submitted.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial approval was granted.

sentences.zh: 坤寧宮祀神昉自盛京。

translations.literal: Worship of spirits at the Palace of Earthly Tranquility began at Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit worship at the Palace of Earthly Tranquility began at Mukden.

sentences.zh: 既建堂子祀天，復設神位清寧宮正寢。

translations.literal: After building the Tangzi to worship Heaven, spirit tablets were also set up in the main chamber of the Palace of Serene Tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tangzi was built for worship of Heaven, spirit tablets were also installed in the main chamber of the Palace of Serene Tranquility.

sentences.zh: 世祖定燕京，率循舊制，定坤寧宮祀神禮。

translations.literal: When the Shizu emperor established Yanjing, he broadly followed the old system and fixed the rites of spirit worship at the Palace of Earthly Tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizu emperor established Yanjing, he broadly followed the old system and fixed the rites of spirit worship at the Palace of Earthly Tranquility.

sentences.zh: 宮廣九楹，東暖閣懸高宗御制銘，略言：「首在盛京，清寧正寢，建極熙鴻，貞符義審。

translations.literal: The palace was nine bays wide; in the east warmed chamber hung an inscription composed by the Gaozong emperor, briefly stating: "First at Mukden, the main chamber of serene tranquility, establishing the utmost and proclaiming great splendor, omen of constancy and righteousness examined.
translations.idiomatic: The palace was nine bays wide; in the east warmed chamber hung an inscription by the Gaozong emperor, which in brief read: "First at Mukden, the main chamber of serene tranquility, establishing the utmost and proclaiming great splendor, the omen of constancy and righteousness examined.

sentences.zh: 思媚嗣徽，松茂竹苞，神罔時恫，執豕酌匏。」

translations.literal: Thinking of pleasing the succession, pine lush and bamboo thick, the spirit never at timid ease, holding the pig and pouring from the gourd."
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of pleasing the succession, pine lush and bamboo thick, the spirit never at timid ease, holding the pig and pouring from the gourd."

sentences.zh: 其眷眷祀神如此。

translations.literal: Thus devoted was the worship of spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the devotion shown in spirit worship.

sentences.zh: 宮西供朝祭神位，北夕祭神位，廷樹桿以祀天。

translations.literal: West of the palace were enshrined the morning-sacrifice spirit tablets; to the north the evening-sacrifice spirit tablets; in the court a pole was set up to worship Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: West of the palace stood the morning-sacrifice spirit tablets; to the north the evening-sacrifice spirit tablets; in the courtyard a pole was erected for worship of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 朝祭神為佛、為關聖，夕祭神為穆哩罕諸神，祝辭所稱納丹岱琿為七星之祀，喀屯諾延為蒙古神，並以先世有功而祀者。

translations.literal: Morning-sacrifice spirits were the Buddha and Lord Guan; evening-sacrifice spirits were the Mulihan spirits; in the blessing text Nadan Daihui was named for worship of the Seven Stars, Kartu Noyan for the Mongol spirits—all worshipped because ancestors of former generations had merit.
translations.idiomatic: The morning-sacrifice spirits were the Buddha and Lord Guan; the evening-sacrifice spirits were the Mulihan spirits; in the blessing text Nadan Daihui named the worship of the Seven Stars and Kartu Noyan the Mongol spirits—all honored because forebears of former generations had rendered merit.

sentences.zh: 餘如年錫、安春阿雅喇諸號，「納爾琿、安哲、鄂囉羅」諸字，雖訓義未詳，而流傳有自。

translations.literal: Other titles such as Nianxi and Anchun Ayala, and words such as "Naerhui, Anzhe, Eluola," though their meanings are not clear in exegesis, have been handed down from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Other titles such as Nianxi and Anchun Ayala, and words such as "Naerhui, Anzhe, Eluola," though their meanings remain unclear in commentary, have been handed down from of old.

sentences.zh: 綜其所祀，曰元旦行禮，曰日祭，曰月祭及翼日祭，曰報祭，曰大祭，曰背鐙祭及翼日祭，曰四季獻神。

translations.literal: Summing up what was worshipped: New Year's Day rites, daily sacrifice, monthly sacrifice and sacrifice on the following day, thanksgiving sacrifice, great sacrifice, back-stirrup sacrifice and sacrifice on the following day, seasonal presentation of spirits in four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: In sum, what was worshipped included: New Year's Day rites, daily sacrifice, monthly sacrifice and sacrifice on the following day, thanksgiving sacrifice, great sacrifice, back-stirrup sacrifice and sacrifice on the following day, and seasonal presentation of spirits in the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 其儀節大率類堂子。

translations.literal: The ritual procedures were in general like those of the Tangzi.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual procedures were in general like those at the Tangzi.

sentences.zh: 茲略舉其小異者。

translations.literal: Here only the minor differences are briefly noted.
translations.idiomatic: Here only the minor differences are briefly set forth.

sentences.zh: 元旦子刻，司香上香，帝、後行禮。

translations.literal: At the midnight hour of New Year's Day the incense officer offered incense and the emperor and empress performed the rite.
translations.idiomatic: At the midnight hour of New Year's Day the incense officer offered incense, and the emperor and empress performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 日祭，順治初，定大內日祭，朝以丑、寅，夕以未、申。

translations.literal: Daily sacrifice: early in Shunzhi, daily sacrifice within the Inner Court was fixed—morning in the chou and yin hours, evening in the wei and shen hours.
translations.idiomatic: Daily sacrifice: early in the Shunzhi reign, daily sacrifice within the Inner Court was fixed—the morning rite in the chou and yin hours, the evening rite in the wei and shen hours.

sentences.zh: 朝祭，司香豫懸黃幔，奉菩薩、關帝像，東鄉。

translations.literal: For the morning sacrifice the incense officer beforehand hung a yellow curtain and enshrined images of the Bodhisattva and Lord Guan, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: For the morning sacrifice the incense officer hung a yellow curtain in advance and enshrined images of the Bodhisattva and Lord Guan, facing east.

sentences.zh: 左、右炕上置低桌二，陳爐、盞各三，時果九，糕十。

translations.literal: On the kang to left and right two low tables were placed, displaying three incense burners and three cups each, nine seasonal fruits, and ten cakes.
translations.idiomatic: On the kang to left and right stood two low tables bearing three incense burners and three cups each, nine seasonal fruits, and ten cakes.

sentences.zh: 炕前置獻案，黃磁碗二，虛其一，以一實酒。

translations.literal: Before the kang an offering table was set out with two yellow porcelain bowls, one left empty and one filled with wine.
translations.idiomatic: Before the kang an offering table was set with two yellow porcelain bowls, one left empty and one filled with wine.

sentences.zh: 案下列樽酒，前設采氈。

translations.literal: Below the table ritual wine in jars was set out, and colored felt was spread in front.
translations.idiomatic: Below the table stood jars of ritual wine, with colored felt spread in front.

sentences.zh: 昧爽，司俎等進二豕，司香獻香，執弦板內監暨司俎官帥屬進，奏神弦，拍板，拊掌應節。

translations.literal: At daybreak the meat-offering officials presented two pigs; the incense officer offered incense; eunuchs holding string boards and the meat-offering official led their subordinates forward, playing the spirit strings and clappers, clapping hands in time.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the meat-offering officials presented two pigs; the incense officer offered incense; eunuchs with string boards and the meat-offering official led their attendants forward, playing spirit strings and clappers and clapping hands in time.

sentences.zh: 司祝跪六獻，酒灌虛碗中，一叩，興，合掌致敬。

translations.literal: The prayer officer knelt and presented six times; wine was poured into the empty bowl; he kowtowed once, rose, and joined his palms in salutation.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer knelt and presented six times, pouring wine into the empty bowl; he kowtowed once, rose, and joined his palms in salutation.

sentences.zh: 餘如堂子朝祭儀。

translations.literal: The remainder followed the morning-sacrifice rite at the Tangzi.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder followed the morning-sacrifice rite at the Tangzi.

sentences.zh: 司祝復跪，一叩，興。

translations.literal: The prayer officer knelt again, kowtowed once, and rose.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer knelt again, kowtowed once, and rose.

sentences.zh: 又誦贊三，弦板止，侍側。

translations.literal: He again recited praise three times; the strings and clappers ceased; he waited at the side.
translations.idiomatic: He recited praise three times again; the strings and clappers fell silent, and he waited at the side.

sentences.zh: 帝親詣，入門，立神位前。

translations.literal: The emperor came in person, entered the gate, and stood before the spirit tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person, entered the gate, and stood before the spirit tablet.

sentences.zh: 司祝先跪，帝跪。

translations.literal: The prayer officer knelt first; the emperor knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer knelt first; then the emperor knelt.

sentences.zh: 司祝致辭，帝行禮，興，司祝叩，興，合掌致敬。

translations.literal: The prayer officer delivered the invocation; the emperor performed the rite and rose; the prayer officer kowtowed, rose, and joined his palms in salutation.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer delivered the invocation; the emperor performed the rite and rose; the prayer officer kowtowed, rose, and joined his palms in salutation.

sentences.zh: 後隨行禮。

translations.literal: The empress followed in performing the rite.
translations.idiomatic: The empress followed in performing the rite.

sentences.zh: 將事者俱退，留司俎、司祝、司香婦人侍行禮。

translations.literal: All who were to perform the service withdrew; the meat-offering official, prayer officer, and incense-offering women remained to assist in the rite.
translations.idiomatic: All who had taken part in the service withdrew, leaving the meat-offering official, prayer officer, and women incense officers to continue the rite.

sentences.zh: 時帝南後北，帝不與祭。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was south and the empress north; the emperor did not participate in the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor stood to the south and the empress to the north; the emperor did not take part in the offering.

sentences.zh: 司祝叩興後，徹琖，奉神像納黃筒，位西楹大亭中。

translations.literal: After the prayer officer's kowtow and rising, the cups were removed, and the spirit image was placed in the yellow tube and positioned in the great pavilion at the west bay.
translations.idiomatic: After the prayer officer kowtowed and rose, the cups were removed and the spirit image was placed in the yellow tube and set in the great pavilion at the west bay.

sentences.zh: 徙幔稍南，安關帝像正中，執弦板者進，跪坐，司香斂氈三折之，奏弦拍板如初。

translations.literal: The curtain was shifted slightly south; the image of Lord Guan was installed in the center; those holding string boards advanced and knelt to sit; the incense officer folded the felt three times and played strings and clappers as before.
translations.idiomatic: The curtain was shifted slightly south; the image of Lord Guan was set in the center; those with string boards advanced and knelt to sit; the incense officer folded the felt three times and played strings and clappers as before.

sentences.zh: 司祝跽氈上，致辭，獻香酒，司祝酌酒，執豕耳灌之，一叩，弦板止。

translations.literal: The prayer officer knelt on the felt, delivered the invocation, and presented incense and wine; the prayer officer poured wine, took the pig's ear and poured libation, kowtowed once; the strings and clappers ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer knelt on the felt, delivered the invocation, and presented incense and wine; he poured wine, lifted the pig's ear to pour libation, and kowtowed once; the strings and clappers fell silent.

sentences.zh: 司祝舉豕於俎、復奏、拍，灌如初，一叩，興，退。

translations.literal: The prayer officer lifted the pig onto the offering table, played and clapped again, poured libation as before, kowtowed once, rose, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer raised the pig onto the offering table, played and clapped again, poured libation as before, kowtowed once, rose, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 司俎如法刲牲，熟而薦之。

translations.literal: The meat-offering official slaughtered the victim according to the rite, cooked it, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: The meat-offering official slaughtered the victim according to the rite, cooked it, and presented it.

sentences.zh: 司香獻香，司俎進跪，凡三獻，俱奏弦、拍板、拊掌。

translations.literal: The incense officer offered incense; the meat-offering official advanced kneeling; in all three presentations strings, clappers, and hand-clapping were performed.
translations.idiomatic: The incense officer offered incense; the meat-offering official advanced kneeling; for all three presentations strings, clappers, and hand-clapping accompanied the rite.

sentences.zh: 畢，徹饌，列胙長案上，或帝率後受胙，或率王、公等食肉，否則大臣侍衛進食之。

translations.literal: When finished, the feast was removed and the sacrificial meat arranged on a long table; either the emperor led the empress in receiving the meat, or led princes and dukes in eating the meat, or else ministers and bodyguards advanced the food.
translations.idiomatic: When finished, the feast was cleared and sacrificial meat set on a long table; either the emperor led the empress to receive the meat, or led princes and dukes to eat it, or ministers and bodyguards served the food.

sentences.zh: 夕祭，司香豫懸青幔，西樹桿，懸大小神鈴七。

translations.literal: For the evening sacrifice the incense officer beforehand hung a blue-green curtain; to the west a pole was set up and seven large and small spirit bells were hung.
translations.idiomatic: For the evening sacrifice the incense officer hung a blue-green curtain in advance; to the west a pole was erected and seven large and small spirit bells were hung.

sentences.zh: 幔內奉穆哩罕神、畫像神、蒙古神，南鄉。

translations.literal: Within the curtain Mulihan spirits, painted spirit images, and Mongol spirits were enshrined, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Within the curtain were enshrined Mulihan spirits, painted spirit images, and Mongol spirits, all facing south.

sentences.zh: 前低桌二，陳爐、琖各五。

translations.literal: In front, two low tables with five incense burners and five cups each.
translations.idiomatic: In front stood two low tables with five incense burners and five cups each.

sentences.zh: 別懸菩薩像西楹大亭，鋪油紙，設案如朝祭。

translations.literal: Separately an image of the Bodhisattva was hung in the great pavilion at the west bay; oiled paper was spread and a table set out as for the morning sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Separately an image of the Bodhisattva was hung in the great pavilion at the west bay; oiled paper was spread and a table set out as for the morning sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 既上香，司祝系裙、束腰鈴、擊手鼓，坐杌上誦神歌祈請曰：「自天而降，阿琿年錫之神，與日分精，年錫之神，年錫唯靈。

translations.literal: After incense was offered, the prayer officer tied on a skirt, bound waist bells, and struck the hand drum; seated on a stool he recited the spirit song of petition, saying: "Descended from Heaven, spirit of Ahui Nianxi, sharing essence with the sun, spirit of Nianxi, Nianxi alone is numinous.
translations.idiomatic: After incense was offered, the prayer officer tied on a skirt, bound waist bells, and struck the hand drum; seated on a stool he recited the spirit song of petition: "Descended from Heaven, spirit of Ahui Nianxi, sharing essence with the sun, spirit of Nianxi—Nianxi alone is numinous.

sentences.zh: 安春阿雅喇、穆哩穆哩哈、納丹岱琿、納爾琿軒初、恩都哩僧固、拜滿章京、納丹威瑚哩、恩都蒙鄂樂、喀屯諾延，某年生小子，今為所乘馬敬祝者」云云。

translations.literal: Anchun Ayala, Mulimuliha, Nadan Daihui, Naerhui Xuan'chu, Enduri Senggu, Baiman Zhangjing, Nadan Weihuli, Endu Meng'e'le, Kartu Noyan—a lad born in such-and-such a year, now in reverent prayer for the horse I ride," and so on.
translations.idiomatic: Anchun Ayala, Mulimuliha, Nadan Daihui, Naerhui Xuan'chu, Enduri Senggu, Baiman Zhangjing, Nadan Weihuli, Endu Meng'e'le, Kartu Noyan—a lad born in such-and-such a year, now in reverent prayer for the horse I ride," and so forth.

sentences.zh: 辭同馬祭，擊鼓拍板和之。

translations.literal: The words were the same as for the horse sacrifice, with drum and clapper keeping time.
translations.idiomatic: The words matched those of the horse sacrifice, with drum and clapper keeping time.

sentences.zh: 初禱曰納丹岱琿、納爾琿軒初，二禱曰恩都哩僧固，三禱曰拜滿章京、納丹威瑚哩、恩都蒙鄂樂、喀屯諾延，三禱並為馬祝云云。

translations.literal: The first prayer named Nadan Daihui and Naerhui Xuan'chu; the second named Enduri Senggu; the third named Baiman Zhangjing, Nadan Weihuli, Endu Meng'e'le, and Kartu Noyan—the third prayer was also a horse blessing, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: The first prayer named Nadan Daihui and Naerhui Xuan'chu; the second named Enduri Senggu; the third named Baiman Zhangjing, Nadan Weihuli, Endu Meng'e'le, and Kartu Noyan—the third prayer was likewise a horse blessing, and so on.

sentences.zh: 皆擊鼓為節，內監亦擊拍板以和，止，退，釋手鼓腰鈴，司香設采氈，帝親行禮如朝祭儀。

translations.literal: All kept time by striking the drum; eunuchs also struck clappers in harmony; when they ceased they withdrew, set aside hand drum and waist bells; the incense officer spread colored felt; the emperor performed the rite in person as in the morning-sacrifice rite.
translations.idiomatic: All kept time by striking the drum; eunuchs also struck clappers in harmony; when they stopped they withdrew, set aside hand drum and waist bells; the incense officer spread colored felt; and the emperor performed the rite in person as in the morning sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 後隨行，則帝東後西。

translations.literal: The empress followed; then the emperor was east and the empress west.
translations.idiomatic: The empress followed; then the emperor stood east and the empress west.

sentences.zh: 刲牲、薦俎暨叩跪、致辭如初。

translations.literal: Slaughtering the victim, presenting on the offering table, kowtowing and kneeling, and delivering the invocation were as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Slaughtering the victim, presenting on the offering table, kneeling and kowtowing, and delivering the invocation were as before.

sentences.zh: 畢。

translations.literal: Finished.
translations.idiomatic: The rite was finished.

sentences.zh: 遇齋期、國忌，不宰牲。

translations.literal: On fast days and national mourning, victims were not slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: On fast days and during national mourning, victims were not slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 並十二月二十六日請神送堂子後，宮內均停祭。

translations.literal: Also after the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth month, when spirits were requested and escorted to the Tangzi, sacrifices within the palace all ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Also after the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth month, once the spirits had been fetched and escorted to the Tangzi, all sacrifices within the palace ceased.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十二年，制定坤寧宮祭神背鐙供獻，其儀，夕祭薦肉後，司香斂氈，展青綢幕，掩鐙火，眾出闔戶，留司祝及執板鼓內監侍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Qianlong, offerings for the back-stirrup spirit worship at the Palace of Earthly Tranquility were fixed; in the rite, after meat was presented at the evening sacrifice, the incense officer folded the felt, spread a blue silk curtain, covered the stirrup lights, all withdrew and closed the doors, leaving the prayer officer and eunuchs holding boards and drums in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Qianlong, back-stirrup offerings for spirit worship at the Palace of Earthly Tranquility were established; after meat was presented at the evening sacrifice, the incense officer folded the felt, spread a blue silk curtain, covered the stirrup lights, all withdrew and closed the doors, leaving the prayer officer and eunuchs with boards and drums in attendance.

sentences.zh: 司祝坐杌上振桿鈴，初向神鈴致祈請，辭曰：「哲，伊埒呼，哲，納爾琿。

translations.literal: The prayer officer sat on a stool and shook the pole bell; first he addressed the spirit bell with a petition, the words saying: "Zhe, Yiliehu, zhe, Naerhui.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer sat on a stool and shook the pole bell; first he addressed the spirit bell in petition, saying: "Zhe, Yiliehu, zhe, Naerhui.

sentences.zh: 掩戶牖以迓神兮，納爾琿。

translations.literal: Closing doors and windows to welcome the spirit—Naerhui.
translations.idiomatic: Closing doors and windows to welcome the spirit—Naerhui.

sentences.zh: 息甑灶以迓神兮，納爾琿。

translations.literal: Stilling kettle and hearth to welcome the spirit—Naerhui.
translations.idiomatic: Stilling kettle and hearth to welcome the spirit—Naerhui.

sentences.zh: 來將迎兮，侑坐以俟，納爾琿。

translations.literal: Coming to welcome—seated in attendance to wait, Naerhui.
translations.idiomatic: Coming to welcome you—seated in attendance to wait, Naerhui.

sentences.zh: 秘以俟兮，几筵具陳，納爾琿。

translations.literal: Secretly waiting—tables and mats fully set out, Naerhui.
translations.idiomatic: Waiting in secret—tables and mats fully set out, Naerhui.

sentences.zh: 納丹岱琿藹然降兮，納爾琿。

translations.literal: Nadan Daihui descends in kindly majesty—Naerhui.
translations.idiomatic: Nadan Daihui descends in kindly majesty—Naerhui.

sentences.zh: 卓爾歡鍾依惠然臨兮，納爾琿。

translations.literal: Zhuo'er Huanzhongyi graciously draws near—Naerhui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo'er Huanzhongyi graciously draws near—Naerhui.

sentences.zh: 感於神靈兮來格，蒞於神鈴兮來歇，納爾琿。」

translations.literal: Moved by the numinous spirits, come to take your place; draw near the spirit bell and come to rest—Naerhui."
translations.idiomatic: Stirred by the numinous spirits, come to take your seat; draw near the spirit bell and come to rest—Naerhui."

sentences.zh: 二次搖神鈴致禱，辭曰：「納丹岱琿、納爾琿軒初、卓爾歡鍾依、珠嚕珠克特亨，某年生小子，今為所乘馬祝者」云云。

translations.literal: A second time he shook the spirit bell and delivered prayer, the words saying: "Nadan Daihui, Naerhui Xuan'chu, Zhuo'er Huanzhongyi, Zhulu Zhuketeheng—a lad born in such-and-such a year, now prayer-offerer for the horse I ride," and so on.
translations.idiomatic: A second time he shook the spirit bell and offered prayer, saying: "Nadan Daihui, Naerhui Xuan'chu, Zhuo'er Huanzhongyi, Zhulu Zhuketeheng—a lad born in such-and-such a year, now in reverent prayer for the horse I ride," and so forth.

sentences.zh: 餘辭同馬祭。

translations.literal: The remaining words were the same as for the horse sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining words matched those of the horse sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 三次向腰鈴致祈請，辭曰：「哲，伊埒呼，哲，古伊雙寬。

translations.literal: A third time he addressed the waist bell with a petition, the words saying: "Zhe, Yiliehu, zhe, Guyishuangkuan.
translations.idiomatic: A third time he addressed the waist bell in petition, saying: "Zhe, Yiliehu, zhe, Guyishuangkuan.

sentences.zh: 列几筵以敬迓，古伊雙寬。

translations.literal: Tables and mats arrayed to welcome in reverence—Guyishuangkuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tables and mats set out to welcome you in reverence—Guyishuangkuan.

sentences.zh: 潔粢盛兮以恭延，古伊雙寬。

translations.literal: Pure grain offerings to extend welcome in respect—Guyishuangkuan.
translations.idiomatic: Pure grain offerings offered to welcome you in respect—Guyishuangkuan.

sentences.zh: 來將迎兮盡敬，古伊雙寬。

translations.literal: Coming to welcome with utmost reverence—Guyishuangkuan.
translations.idiomatic: Coming to welcome you with utmost reverence—Guyishuangkuan.

sentences.zh: 秘以俟兮申虔，古伊雙寬。

translations.literal: Waiting in secret to declare devotion—Guyishuangkuan.
translations.idiomatic: Waiting in secret to declare our devotion—Guyishuangkuan.

sentences.zh: 乘羽葆兮陟於位，古伊雙寬。

translations.literal: Riding the feather canopy, ascending to the seat—Guyishuangkuan.
translations.idiomatic: Borne on the feather canopy, ascending to your seat—Guyishuangkuan.

sentences.zh: 應鈴響兮降於壇，古伊雙寬。」

translations.literal: At the bell's sounding, descending to the altar—Guyishuangkuan."
translations.idiomatic: At the bell's answer, descending to the altar—Guyishuangkuan."

sentences.zh: 四次搖腰鈴，復致禱，辭曰：「籥者唯神，迓者斐孫，犧牲既陳，奔走臣鄰。

translations.literal: A fourth time he shook the waist bell and again delivered prayer, the words saying: "The pipes are for the spirits alone; the welcomer is Feisun; victims are already set out; ministers and neighbors hasten in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: A fourth time he shook the waist bell and prayed again, saying: "The pipes belong to the spirits alone; Feisun is the welcomer; victims stand ready; ministers and neighbors hasten to attend.

sentences.zh: 仍為所乘馬敬祝者」云云。

translations.literal: Still in reverent prayer for the horse I ride," and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: Still in reverent prayer for the horse I ride," and so on.

sentences.zh: 每次並擊鼓拍板以和。

translations.literal: Each time the drum and clappers were struck together to keep time.
translations.idiomatic: Each time drum and clappers were struck together to keep the measure.

sentences.zh: 畢，啟扉明鐙，司俎徹俎，司香卷幔，奉神像納硃匱。

translations.literal: When finished, they opened the doors and brightened the stirrup lights; the meat-offering officer removed the offering table; the incense officer rolled up the curtain; the spirit image was placed in the cinnabar case.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished, they opened the doors and lit the stirrup lamps; the meat-offering officer cleared the offering table; the incense officer rolled up the curtain; and the spirit image was enshrined in the cinnabar case.

sentences.zh: 月祭略同日祭，唯食品因月而殊，灌豕耳以酒不以水。

translations.literal: Monthly sacrifice was largely the same as daily sacrifice, save that foods varied with the month, and the pig's ear was libated with wine, not water.
translations.idiomatic: The monthly sacrifice largely followed the daily rite, save that foods varied with the month and the pig's ear was libated with wine rather than water.

sentences.zh: 如為皇子祭祀，則司祝禱祝，皇子叩拜。

translations.literal: If the sacrifice was for an imperial son, the prayer officer prayed and the imperial son kowtowed.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrifice was performed for an imperial son, the prayer officer offered prayer and the imperial son kowtowed.

sentences.zh: 翼日祭天，安佛、菩薩像西楹大亭，神桿東北置案一，西鄉。
