translations.literal: On the following day Heaven was sacrificed to; images of the Buddha and Bodhisattva were installed in the great pavilion at the west bay; one table was placed northeast of the spirit pole, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day they sacrificed to Heaven; images of the Buddha and the Bodhisattva were installed in the great pavilion at the west bay; one table was set northeast of the spirit pole, facing west.

sentences.zh: 奉桿倚柱座前，桿首鄉東仰。

translations.literal: The pole was presented and leaned before the pillar seat; the pole head faced east and tilted upward.
translations.idiomatic: The pole was set before the pillar seat and leaned there; its head faced east and tilted skyward.

sentences.zh: 案陳銀盤三，一實米居中。

translations.literal: On the table three silver dishes were set out, one filled with rice placed in the center.
translations.idiomatic: Three silver dishes were set on the table, with one filled with rice placed at the center.

sentences.zh: 西北置幔架，覆紅罽。

translations.literal: To the northwest a curtain frame was placed, covered with red felt.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest stood a curtain frame draped with red felt.

sentences.zh: 東北置牲案。

translations.literal: To the northeast a victim table was placed.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast a victim table was set.

sentences.zh: 昧爽，司俎進一豕。

translations.literal: At daybreak the meat-offering official presented one pig.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the meat-offering official presented a pig.

sentences.zh: 司香設采氈閾內，帝行禮，鄉神桿南面跪。

translations.literal: The incense officer spread colored felt within the threshold; the emperor performed the rite, kneeling facing south toward the spirit pole.
translations.idiomatic: The incense officer spread colored felt inside the threshold; the emperor performed the rite, kneeling south toward the spirit pole.

sentences.zh: 司俎進，舉盤中米灑之。

translations.literal: The meat-offering official advanced and, lifting the rice in the dish, sprinkled it.
translations.idiomatic: The meat-offering official advanced, lifted the rice from the dish, and sprinkled it.

sentences.zh: 祝禱畢，興。

translations.literal: When the blessing prayer was finished, he rose.
translations.idiomatic: When the blessing prayer was finished, he rose.

sentences.zh: 不親祭，則司祝奉御衣叩拜。

translations.literal: If he did not sacrifice in person, the prayer officer held the imperial robe and performed the kowtow.
translations.idiomatic: If he did not sacrifice in person, the prayer officer held the imperial robe and performed the kowtow on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 後隨行，帝居中，後傍西。

translations.literal: The empress followed; the emperor stood in the center and the empress to the west beside him.
translations.idiomatic: The empress followed in the rite; the emperor stood at the center and the empress to the west beside him.

sentences.zh: 刲牲熟薦，陳頸、膽左右銀盤，縷肉為膾，列碗二，佐以箸；

translations.literal: The victim was slaughtered, cooked, and presented; neck and gall were set on silver dishes to left and right; meat was shredded for kuai, arranged in two bowls with chopsticks as aides;
translations.idiomatic: The victim was slaughtered, cooked, and presented; neck and gall were set on silver dishes to left and right; meat was shredded for kuai and set in two bowls with chopsticks beside them;

sentences.zh: 炊稗為飯，列碗二，佐以匙；

translations.literal: broomcorn millet was steamed for rice, arranged in two bowls with spoons as aides;
translations.idiomatic: broomcorn millet was steamed into rice and set in two bowls with spoons beside them;

sentences.zh: 相間以獻。

translations.literal: and presented alternately.
translations.idiomatic: and the offerings were presented in alternation.

sentences.zh: 帝復行禮，灑米如初。

translations.literal: The emperor again performed the rite, sprinkling rice as at first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again performed the rite, sprinkling rice as before.

sentences.zh: 禮成，司俎奉頸骨桿端，膽、膾及米置桿碗，桿遂立。

translations.literal: When the rite was finished, the meat-offering official placed the neck bone at the pole's end; gall, kuai, and rice were placed in the pole bowl, and the pole was raised upright.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, the meat-offering official set the neck bone at the pole's end; gall, kuai, and rice were placed in the pole bowl, and the pole was raised upright.

sentences.zh: 以所獻肉飯進，帝後受胙，退。

translations.literal: The presented meat and rice were advanced; emperor and empress received the sacrificial portion and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The presented meat and rice were brought forward; the emperor and empress received the sacrificial portion and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 如為皇子祭天，則皇子叩拜。

translations.literal: If Heaven was sacrificed to for an imperial son, the imperial son kowtowed.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven was sacrificed to on behalf of an imperial son, the imperial son kowtowed.

sentences.zh: 不親祭，則司祝奉皇子衣服叩拜。

translations.literal: If he did not sacrifice in person, the prayer officer held the imperial son's garments and performed the kowtow.
translations.idiomatic: If he did not sacrifice in person, the prayer officer held the imperial son's garments and performed the kowtow on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 報祭，歲春、秋二季，立桿大祭。

translations.literal: Thanksgiving sacrifice: in spring and autumn of the year, the great sacrifice with pole raised.
translations.idiomatic: The thanksgiving sacrifice fell in spring and autumn each year—a great rite with the spirit pole raised.

sentences.zh: 前期四旬，釀酒西炕上，祭前一日漉之。

translations.literal: Forty days beforehand wine was brewed on the west kang; on the day before the sacrifice it was strained.
translations.idiomatic: Forty days beforehand wine was brewed on the west kang; on the eve of the sacrifice it was strained.

sentences.zh: 司香染布為神冠，制楮帛。

translations.literal: The incense officer dyed cloth for spirit caps and prepared paper and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The incense officer dyed cloth into spirit caps and prepared paper and silk offerings.

sentences.zh: 大祭日，司俎婦人打糕作穆丹條子，餘如前儀。

translations.literal: On the day of the great sacrifice, women of the meat-offering office pounded cakes into Mudan strips; the remainder followed the earlier rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the great sacrifice, women of the meat-offering office pounded cakes into Mudan strips; the rest followed the earlier rite.

sentences.zh: 其翼日祭天，與月祭翼日同。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to Heaven on the following day was the same as the monthly sacrifice's following day.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrifice to Heaven on the following day was the same as that on the day after the monthly sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 四孟月大祭，亦曰四季獻神，懸朝祭、夕祭神幔，並同日祭儀。

translations.literal: Great sacrifice in the four first months of the seasons, also called presentation of spirits in the four seasons, hung morning- and evening-sacrifice spirit curtains, all together with the daily sacrifice rite.
translations.idiomatic: The great sacrifice in the four seasonal first months, also called presentation of spirits in the four quarters, hung curtains for the morning and evening spirits and followed the daily sacrifice rite throughout.

sentences.zh: 涓吉，具馬二，牛一，金、銀錠各二，蟒緞、龍緞、片金倭緞、閃緞、各色緞十，毛青布十，置案。

translations.literal: An auspicious day was selected; two horses, one ox, two gold ingots and two silver ingots, python-patterned satin, dragon satin, brocaded Japanese satin with gold flakes, shimmering satin, ten bolts of satin in assorted colors, and ten bolts of gray-blue cloth were prepared and set on the table.
translations.idiomatic: An auspicious day was chosen; two horses, one ox, two gold and two silver ingots, python satin, dragon satin, gold-flaked Japanese brocade, shimmering satin, ten bolts of assorted-colored satin, and ten bolts of gray-blue cloth were prepared and laid on the table.

sentences.zh: 掌儀官等前引，內府大臣、上駟院卿同行。

translations.literal: Masters of ceremony and others led the way; the Inner Palace grand minister and the Director of the Imperial Stud walked together.
translations.idiomatic: Masters of ceremony led the way, and the minister of the Imperial Household and the Director of the Imperial Stud walked together.

sentences.zh: 自乾清右門舁入，逕交泰殿，至坤寧宮門外。

translations.literal: They were carried in through the right gate of the Palace of Heavenly Purity, passed straight through the Hall of Union, to outside the gate of the Palace of Earthly Tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: They were borne in through the right gate of the Palace of Heavenly Purity, passed straight through the Hall of Union, and halted outside the gate of the Palace of Earthly Tranquility.

sentences.zh: 陳馬於西，列牛於東。

translations.literal: Horses were arranged to the west, oxen lined to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Horses were arrayed to the west and oxen to the east.

sentences.zh: 司俎等奉金銀緞布入，司香陳案上，奉朝祭神位前，加金銀其上。

translations.literal: Meat-offering officials and others brought in gold, silver, satin, and cloth; the incense officer set them on the table and presented them before the morning-sacrifice spirit seat, placing gold and silver atop.
translations.idiomatic: Meat-offering officials brought in the gold, silver, satin, and cloth; the incense officer set them on the table and presented them before the morning-sacrifice spirit seat, with gold and silver placed on top.

sentences.zh: 司祝跪致辭，一叩，興。

translations.literal: The prayer officer knelt and delivered the invocation, kowtowed once, and rose.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer knelt, delivered the invocation, kowtowed once, and rose.

sentences.zh: 復舉案夕祭神位前，如上儀。

translations.literal: He again raised the table before the evening-sacrifice spirit seat, according to the rite above.
translations.idiomatic: He again raised the table before the evening-sacrifice spirit seat, following the rite above.

sentences.zh: 帝親祭，禮同月朔。

translations.literal: The emperor sacrificed in person; the rite was the same as on the first day of the month.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sacrificed in person, and the rite matched that of the first day of the month.

sentences.zh: 陳獻畢，司香舉金銀緞布貯案下，侍衛等牽牛馬出。

translations.literal: When presentation was finished, the incense officer took the gold, silver, satin, and cloth and stored them beneath the table; bodyguards and others led the oxen and horses out.
translations.idiomatic: When the presentation was finished, the incense officer took the gold, silver, satin, and cloth and stored them under the table; bodyguards led the oxen and horses away.

sentences.zh: 越三日，宮殿監諸神位前，以金銀緞布及牛馬授會計司發售，計直購豕以祭。

translations.literal: Three days later, before the various spirit seats, the Palace Directorate turned over the gold, silver, satin, cloth, oxen, and horses to the accounting office for sale, reckoned the proceeds, and purchased pigs for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later, before the spirit seats, the Palace Directorate handed the gold, silver, satin, cloth, oxen, and horses to the accounting office to be sold; the proceeds were reckoned and pigs purchased for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 故事，帝獵南苑或他所，射得狍、鹿，如尾氾腑臟無傷者，雖小創必整潔之，備供獻，傷多體缺者舍之。

translations.literal: By precedent, when the emperor hunted the Southern Park or elsewhere and shot roe deer or stag, if tail, bladder, and viscera were unharmed, though there were small wounds they were surely cleaned and prepared for offering; those with many wounds and maimed bodies were discarded.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when the emperor hunted the Southern Park or elsewhere and took roe deer or stag, if tail, bladder, and viscera were whole, even small wounds were cleaned and the carcass prepared for offering; beasts badly wounded or maimed were set aside.

sentences.zh: 至四時進獻，按時以奉，春雛雞二，夏子鵝一，秋魚一，冬雉二，選肥且澤者以將誠焉。

translations.literal: At the seasonal presentations for the four quarters, offerings were made according to the season: spring two pullets, summer one gosling, autumn one fish, winter two pheasants—selecting those fat and sleek to convey sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: At the four seasonal presentations, offerings followed the season: spring two pullets, summer one gosling, autumn one fish, winter two pheasants—the fattest and sleekest chosen to bear sincerity.

sentences.zh: 令節設供萬壽節、元旦節，宮殿監率各首領設供案天香亭內，北鄉。

translations.literal: For festival observances on Longevity Day and New Year's Day, the Palace Directorate led the various chiefs in setting offering tables inside the Heavenly Fragrance Pavilion, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: For festival observances on Longevity Day and New Year's Day, the Palace Directorate led the chiefs in setting offering tables within the Heavenly Fragrance Pavilion, facing north.

sentences.zh: 奉安神牌、香屬、鐙爐、斗香、拜褥各具，陳祭品七十有五。

translations.literal: Spirit tablets, censers, stirrup braziers, bowl incense, and kneeling cushions were each enshrined; seventy-five offering items were set out.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit tablets, censers, stirrup braziers, bowl incense, and kneeling cushions were each set in place, and seventy-five offering items were displayed.

sentences.zh: 屆時帝拈香行禮，畢，送燎還宮。

translations.literal: At the appointed time the emperor plucked incense and performed the rite; when finished, he escorted to the burning and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the appointed hour the emperor took incense and performed the rite; when it was finished, he escorted the offerings to the fire and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 冬至、夏至或未親行郊禮，則設供宮中。

translations.literal: On winter solstice or summer solstice, or if he had not performed suburban rites in person, offerings were set within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the winter or summer solstice, or when he had not performed the suburban rites in person, offerings were set within the palace.

sentences.zh: 宮殿監設供案，冬至北鄉，夏至南鄉。

translations.literal: The Palace Directorate set offering tables—facing north at winter solstice, south at summer solstice.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Directorate set offering tables—facing north at the winter solstice and south at the summer solstice.

sentences.zh: 奉安神牌、祭品同，拈香送燎亦如之。

translations.literal: Spirit tablets were enshrined and offerings were the same; plucking incense and escorting to the burning were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit tablets were enshrined and the offerings were the same; taking incense and escorting the offerings to the fire followed the same form.

sentences.zh: 立春、立夏、立秋、立冬設案如前儀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of spring, summer, autumn, and winter, tables were set as in the rite above.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginnings of spring, summer, autumn, and winter, tables were set as in the rite above.

sentences.zh: 春東鄉，夏南鄉，秋西鄉，冬北鄉。

translations.literal: Spring faced east, summer south, autumn west, winter north.
translations.idiomatic: In spring they faced east, in summer south, in autumn west, and in winter north.

sentences.zh: 陳祭品三十有六，羊、豕各一，儀如初。

translations.literal: Thirty-six offering items were set out, one sheep and one pig each; the rite was as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-six offering items were set out, with one sheep and one pig; the rite was as before.

sentences.zh: 仲春朔祭日，仲秋望祭月，七月七夕祭牛、女，陳祭品四十有九。

translations.literal: On the first day of mid-spring the sun was sacrificed to; on the full moon of mid-autumn the moon; on the seventh day of the seventh month the Cowherd and Weaver; forty-nine offering items were set out.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of mid-spring they sacrificed to the sun; on the full moon of mid-autumn to the moon; on the seventh day of the seventh month to the Cowherd and Weaver Maid; forty-nine offering items were set out.

sentences.zh: 帝行禮畢，宮殿監奏請皇后、皇貴妃、貴妃、妃、嬪行禮，畢，帝送燎還宮。

translations.literal: When the emperor had finished the rite, the Palace Directorate memorialized requesting that the empress, imperial noble consort, noble consort, consort, and concubine perform the rite; when finished, the emperor escorted to the burning and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had finished the rite, the Palace Directorate memorialized asking that the empress, imperial noble consort, noble consort, consort, and concubine perform the rite; when they had finished, the emperor escorted the offerings to the fire and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 求福祀神所稱佛立佛多鄂謨錫瑪瑪者，知為保嬰而祀也，亦名換索。

translations.literal: The spirit worshipped in the prayer-for-blessings sacrifice, called Folifudo Emuximama, was known to be worshipped for protecting infants; it was also named Exchanging Cords.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit of the prayer-for-blessings rite, called Folifudo Emuximama, was understood to be worshipped for the protection of infants; it was also known as Exchanging Cords.

sentences.zh: 其儀，諏吉有期，豫釀醴酒。

translations.literal: In its rite, an auspicious day was fixed after divination, and sacral wine was brewed in advance.
translations.idiomatic: In this rite an auspicious day was chosen by divination, and sacral wine was brewed beforehand.

sentences.zh: 前期數日，選無事故滿洲九家，攢取棉線綢片，捻線索二紐，小方戒綢三。

translations.literal: Several days beforehand, nine Manchu households without misfortune were selected; they gathered cotton thread and silk scraps, twisted two cords of thread, and three small square ritual silks.
translations.idiomatic: Several days beforehand nine Manchu households free of misfortune were chosen; they gathered cotton thread and silk scraps, twisted two cords, and prepared three small square ritual silks.

sentences.zh: 先一日，司俎官偕奉宸苑官赴西苑斫取柳條全株，高九尺，圍徑三寸。

translations.literal: On the day before, the meat-offering officer together with an officer of the Imperial Parks went to the Western Park to cut a whole willow branch, nine feet high and three inches in girth.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve, the meat-offering officer and an officer of the Imperial Parks went to the Western Park to cut a whole willow branch nine feet high and three inches around.

sentences.zh: 屆期赴坤寧宮廊下，樹柳枝於石，懸淨紙、戒綢。

translations.literal: At the appointed time they went to the corridor of the Palace of Earthly Tranquility, planted the willow branch in stone, and hung pure paper and ritual silk.
translations.idiomatic: At the appointed time they went to the corridor of the Palace of Earthly Tranquility, planted the willow branch in stone, and hung pure paper and ritual silk.

sentences.zh: 幔懸神像。

translations.literal: A curtain was hung and the spirit image enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: A curtain was hung and the spirit image enshrined.

sentences.zh: 炕上設低案一，陳香碟、醴酒各三，豆糕、煤糕、打糕各九。

translations.literal: On the kang one low table was set, displaying three incense dishes and three of sacral wine, nine bean cakes, nine coal cakes, and nine pounded cakes each.
translations.idiomatic: On the kang stood one low table bearing three incense dishes and three of sacral wine, with nine bean cakes, nine coal cakes, and nine pounded cakes each.

sentences.zh: 西炕設求福高案，陳鯉魚、稗米飯、水訄子各二，醴酒、豆糕等皆九數。

translations.literal: On the west kang a tall table for prayer-for-blessings was set, displaying two each of carp, broomcorn millet rice, and water qiuzi; sacral wine, bean cakes, and the rest were all in counts of nine.
translations.idiomatic: On the west kang a tall table for prayer-for-blessings was set with two each of carp, broomcorn millet rice, and water qiuzi; sacral wine, bean cakes, and the rest were all in counts of nine.

sentences.zh: 稍北植神箭，懸線索其上，用三色綢片夾系之，令穿出戶，系之柳枝。

translations.literal: Slightly to the north a spirit arrow was planted; cords were hung upon it, clasped with three-colored silk scraps, made to pass out through the door, and tied to the willow branch.
translations.idiomatic: Slightly to the north a spirit arrow was planted; cords were hung from it, bound with three-colored silk scraps, passed out through the door, and tied to the willow branch.

sentences.zh: 司香展采氈，帝、後親詣行禮，如朝祭儀。

translations.literal: The incense officer spread colored felt; the emperor and empress came in person to perform the rite as in the morning sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The incense officer spread colored felt; the emperor and empress came in person to perform the rite, as at the morning sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 內監司俎官率屬進，奏神弦，鳴拍板，司祝執神刀進，誦神歌禱辭曰：「聚九家之采線，樹柳枝以牽繩。

translations.literal: Eunuchs and the meat-offering official led their attendants forward, playing the spirit strings and sounding clappers; the prayer officer advanced holding the spirit knife and recited the spirit song of petition, saying: "Gathering the colored threads of nine households, planting the willow branch to draw the cord.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs and the meat-offering official led their attendants forward, playing spirit strings and clappers; the prayer officer advanced with the spirit knife and recited the spirit song of petition: "Gathering the colored threads of nine households, planting the willow branch to draw the cord.

sentences.zh: 舉揚神箭，以祈福佑，以致敬誠。

translations.literal: Raising the spirit arrow to seek blessing and protection, thereby rendering reverent sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Raising the spirit arrow to seek blessing and protection, and thereby show reverent sincerity.

sentences.zh: 某年生小子，綏以多福，承之於首，介以繁祉，服之於膺。

translations.literal: A lad born in such-and-such a year—may many blessings soothe him; worn upon the head, may abundant fortune attend; worn upon the breast.
translations.idiomatic: A lad born in such-and-such a year—may he be soothed with many blessings; worn upon the head, may abundant fortune attend him; worn upon the breast.

sentences.zh: 千祥薈集，九敘阜盈。

translations.literal: A thousand auspices gathered together; the nine orders heaped full.
translations.idiomatic: May a thousand auspices gather; may the nine orders overflow.

sentences.zh: 亦既孔皆，福祿來成。

translations.literal: All brought to fullness; fortune and emolument come to completion.
translations.idiomatic: May all be brought to fullness; may fortune and emolument be made complete.

sentences.zh: 神兮貺我，神兮佑我。

translations.literal: Spirit, grant me; spirit, protect me.
translations.idiomatic: O spirit, grant me; O spirit, protect me.

sentences.zh: 豐於首而仔於肩，衛於後而護於前。

translations.literal: Abundant upon the head and sustaining upon the shoulder; guarding behind and shielding before.
translations.idiomatic: Abundant upon the head and firm upon the shoulder; guarding behind and shielding before.

sentences.zh: 畀以嘉祥兮，偕老而成雙兮。

translations.literal: Bestow auspicious blessing; grow old together and become a pair.
translations.idiomatic: Bestow auspicious blessing; may we grow old together and become a pair.

sentences.zh: 富厚而成雙兮，富厚而豐穰兮。

translations.literal: Rich and abundant as a pair; rich, abundant, and overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: Rich and paired in abundance; rich, abundant, and overflowing.

sentences.zh: 如葉之茂兮，如木之榮兮。

translations.literal: Like leaves in luxuriant growth; like trees in flourishing glory.
translations.idiomatic: Like leaves in luxuriant growth; like trees in flourishing glory.

sentences.zh: 食則體腴兮，飲則滋營兮。

translations.literal: In eating, the body grows plump; in drinking, nourishment is replenished.
translations.idiomatic: In eating may the body grow plump; in drinking may nourishment be renewed.

sentences.zh: 甘旨其獻兮，硃顏其鮮兮。

translations.literal: Sweet offerings presented; the cinnabar countenance fresh and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet offerings are presented; the cinnabar countenance fresh and bright.

sentences.zh: 歲其增而根其固兮，年其永而壽其延兮。」

translations.literal: Years increase and roots grow firm; years endure and life is prolonged.
translations.idiomatic: May the years increase and the roots grow firm; may the years endure and life be prolonged.

sentences.zh: 如是者三，眾歌「鄂囉羅」和之。

translations.literal: Thus three times; the assembly sang "Eluola" in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Thus three times, while the assembly sang "Eluola" in answer.

sentences.zh: 禱畢，司香舉線索、神箭授司祝，司香舁高案出戶外，列柳枝前。

translations.literal: When prayer was finished, the incense officer raised the cords and spirit arrow and handed them to the prayer officer; the incense officer carried the tall table outdoors and set it before the willow branch.
translations.idiomatic: When the prayer was finished, the incense officer raised the cords and spirit arrow and handed them to the prayer officer; the incense officer carried the tall table outdoors and set it before the willow branch.

sentences.zh: 司祝左執神刀，右執神箭，立案前。

translations.literal: The prayer officer held the spirit knife in his left hand and the spirit arrow in his right, standing before the table.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer held the spirit knife in his left hand and the spirit arrow in his right, and stood before the table.

sentences.zh: 帝立正中，後立檻內東次。

translations.literal: The emperor stood in the center; the empress stood inside the threshold to the east.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stood at the center; the empress stood within the threshold to the east.

sentences.zh: 皆跪，司祝對柳枝舉揚神箭，以練麻拭其枝。

translations.literal: All knelt; the prayer officer faced the willow branch and raised the spirit arrow, wiping its branch with bleached hemp.
translations.idiomatic: All knelt; the prayer officer faced the willow branch, raised the spirit arrow, and wiped the branch with bleached hemp.

sentences.zh: 初次誦禱畢，舉箭奉練麻進，帝三埒而懷之，歌如前。

translations.literal: When the first recitation of prayer was finished, he raised the arrow and advanced presenting the bleached hemp; the emperor drew three strokes and clasped it to his breast; the song was as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the first prayer was finished, he raised the arrow and advanced with the bleached hemp; the emperor drew three strokes and clasped it to his breast, while the song was sung as before.

sentences.zh: 帝、後一叩，興，柳枝上灑以酒，夾以糕，司祝揚箭歌禱如式。

translations.literal: Emperor and empress kowtowed once and rose; wine was sprinkled on the willow branch and cakes placed between; the prayer officer raised the arrow and sang prayer as in the form.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress kowtowed once and rose; wine was sprinkled on the willow branch and cakes set between; the prayer officer raised the arrow and sang the prayer in the prescribed form.

sentences.zh: 凡三。

translations.literal: In all, three times.
translations.idiomatic: This was done three times in all.

sentences.zh: 帝詣神位前跪，司祝以箭上線索二分奉帝、後，致辭，叩，興，合掌致敬。

translations.literal: The emperor went to kneel before the spirit seat; the prayer officer divided the cords on the arrow in two and presented them to emperor and empress, delivered the invocation, kowtowed, rose, and joined his palms in salutation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to kneel before the spirit seat; the prayer officer divided the cords on the arrow in two and presented them to the emperor and empress, delivered the invocation, kowtowed, rose, and joined his palms in salutation.

sentences.zh: 帝、後同一叩，興。

translations.literal: Emperor and empress kowtowed once together and rose.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress kowtowed once together and rose.

sentences.zh: 司祝進神胙，帝、後受之，還宮。

translations.literal: The prayer officer advanced the spirit portion; emperor and empress received it and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer officer advanced the spirit portion; the emperor and empress received it and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 祀肉與糕不出門，則分給諸人，令戶內盡食之。

translations.literal: If the sacrificial meat and cakes did not leave the door, they were distributed among the attendants, with orders that all within the household eat them completely.
translations.idiomatic: If the sacrificial meat and cakes did not leave the door, they were divided among the attendants, with orders that all within the household consume them entirely.

sentences.zh: 其夕祭求福，帝、後行禮如夕祭儀。

translations.literal: For the evening sacrifice of prayer-for-blessings, emperor and empress performed the rite as in the evening-sacrifice rite.
translations.idiomatic: For the evening prayer-for-blessings sacrifice, the emperor and empress performed the rite as at the evening sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 柳枝所系線索貯於囊，懸西壁上。

translations.literal: The cords tied to the willow branch were stored in a bag and hung on the west wall.
translations.idiomatic: The cords tied to the willow branch were kept in a bag and hung on the west wall.

sentences.zh: 其枝司俎官齎送堂子。

translations.literal: The meat-offering official in charge of the branch conveyed it to the Tangzi.
translations.idiomatic: The meat-offering official charged with the branch carried it to the Tangzi.

sentences.zh: 至除夕，與神桿紙帛爇化之。

translations.literal: On New Year's Eve they were burned together with the spirit pole, paper, and silk.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Eve they were burned together with the spirit pole, paper, and silk.

sentences.zh: 奉先殿順治十三年，詔建景運門東北，前後各九楹，如太廟寢制。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi, for the Hall of Ancestors an edict ordered construction northeast of the Jingyun Gate, nine bays front and rear, following the sleeping-hall form of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 13 the Hall of Ancestors was ordered built northeast of Jingyun Gate—nine bays front and rear—on the model of the Imperial Ancestral Temple sleeping hall.

sentences.zh: 中為堂，左神庫，右神廚。

translations.literal: The center was the hall; to the left the spirit storehouse, to the right the spirit kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: The center served as the hall, with the spirit storehouse on the left and the spirit kitchen on the right.

sentences.zh: 明年殿成，世祖躬妥神位，讀祝大饗。

translations.literal: The following year, when the hall was completed, the Founding Emperor personally installed the spirit seats and read the invocation at the great offering.
translations.idiomatic: When the hall was finished the next year, the Founding Emperor personally installed the spirit seats and read the invocation at the great offering.

sentences.zh: 定制，元旦、冬至、歲除、萬壽、冊封、月朔、望，奉神位前殿，帝親行禮，供獻如太廟大饗儀。

translations.literal: By regulation, on New Year's Day, the winter solstice, year's end, Longevity celebrations, investiture, the first and fifteenth of the month, the spirit seats were brought to the front hall; the emperor personally performed the rite, with offerings as in the Imperial Ancestral Temple great-offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation, on New Year's Day, the winter solstice, year's end, Longevity Day, investiture, and the first and fifteenth of each month, the spirit seats were placed in the front hall and the emperor personally performed the rite, with offerings matching the Imperial Ancestral Temple great offering.

sentences.zh: 唯立春、上元、四月八日、端陽、重陽皆尋常節，國忌、清明、霜降、十月朔屬哀慕期，親祭，不贊禮、作樂。

translations.literal: Only Beginning of Spring, First Full Moon, the eighth day of the fourth month, Dragon Boat Festival, and Double Ninth were ordinary festivals; national mourning, Pure Brightness, Frost's Descent, and the first of the tenth month fell within the period of filial grief—personal sacrifice was performed, without ritual praise or music.
translations.idiomatic: Only Beginning of Spring, Lantern Festival, the eighth day of the fourth month, Dragon Boat Festival, and Double Ninth were treated as ordinary festivals; national mourning days, Pure Brightness, Frost's Descent, and the first of the tenth month were periods of filial observance—the emperor sacrificed in person but without ritual praise or music.

sentences.zh: 七夕如常供。

translations.literal: The Seventh Night had offerings as usual.
translations.idiomatic: On the Seventh Night offerings were made as usual.

sentences.zh: 四月八日、七月望日陳素果。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the fourth month and the full moon of the seventh month plain fruit was set out.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the fourth month and the seventh-month full moon, plain fruit was presented.

sentences.zh: 月薦新，帝親獻。

translations.literal: Monthly presentation of new produce: the emperor personally offered.
translations.idiomatic: When new produce was presented each month, the emperor offered in person.

sentences.zh: 凡常例供獻，後殿行之。

translations.literal: All routine offerings were performed in the rear hall.
translations.idiomatic: All regular offerings were carried out in the rear hall.

sentences.zh: 饗太廟畢，行躬告禮，上香燭。

translations.literal: When the Imperial Ancestral Temple feast was finished, the personal announcement rite was performed and incense and candles were offered.
translations.idiomatic: After the Imperial Ancestral Temple feast, the emperor performed the personal announcement rite and offered incense and candles.

sentences.zh: 又定日供湯、飯、果、肉各五盤。

translations.literal: It was further fixed that daily offerings were soup, rice, fruit, and meat, five platters each.
translations.idiomatic: Daily offerings were also fixed at five platters each of soup, rice, fruit, and meat.

sentences.zh: 元旦、萬壽，請太廟後殿四祖、四後神位至奉先殿，與列聖、列後合饗。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day and Longevity Day, the spirit seats of the four founding ancestors and four founding consorts from the rear hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple were invited to the Hall of Ancestors to join in a combined feast with the successive sages and consorts.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day and Longevity Day, the spirit seats of the four founding ancestors and four founding consorts from the Imperial Ancestral Temple rear hall were brought to the Hall of Ancestors for a combined feast with all successive emperors and empresses.

sentences.zh: 其後罷奉請，就太廟後殿祀之。

translations.literal: Thereafter the invitation was discontinued and they were worshipped in the rear hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Later the invitation was discontinued and they were worshipped in the Imperial Ancestral Temple rear hall instead.

sentences.zh: 是歲冬，御經筵，上親祭焉。

translations.literal: That winter, when the emperor attended the classics lecture, he personally sacrificed there.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, while attending the classics lecture, the emperor personally sacrificed there.

sentences.zh: 十七年，以並夾室乖制，諭令夾室行廊外中通為敞殿九楹，迺改建如旨。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, because combining side-chambers violated regulation, an edict ordered that beyond the side-chambers and connecting corridors a central open hall of nine bays be made, and reconstruction followed the command.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17, combining side-chambers was held to violate regulation; an edict ordered a central open hall of nine bays beyond the side-chambers and connecting corridors, and the hall was rebuilt accordingly.

sentences.zh: 明年，聖祖嗣服，用禮臣言，依明洪武三年例，朝夕焚香，朔、望瞻拜，時節獻新，生、忌致祭，具常饌，行家人禮。

translations.literal: The following year the Sacred Ancestor succeeded to the throne; following the ritual officials, by the Hongwu 3 precedent of Ming, morning and evening incense was burned, obeisance paid on the first and full moon, seasonal new produce presented, sacrifices on birth and death anniversaries, regular viands set out, and the rites of a family household performed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Sacred Ancestor took the throne; following the ritual officials and the Ming Hongwu 3 precedent, he burned incense morning and evening, paid obeisance on new and full moon, presented seasonal produce, sacrificed on birth and death anniversaries, set out regular food, and observed household rites.

sentences.zh: 其冬世祖升祔，奉神位至前殿行大饗。

translations.literal: That winter, when the Founding Emperor was enshrined, the spirit seats were brought to the front hall for the great offering.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the Founding Emperor was enshrined, the spirit seats were carried to the front hall for the great offering.

sentences.zh: 禮成，還奉後殿神龕。

translations.literal: When the rite was finished, they were returned to the spirit shrines of the rear hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, the seats were returned to the rear-hall spirit shrines.

sentences.zh: 厥後祔饗仿此。

translations.literal: Thereafter enshrinement feasts followed this model.
translations.idiomatic: Later enshrinement feasts followed the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，罷日供食，早、晚燃香燭。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, daily food offerings were discontinued; morning and evening only incense and candles were burned.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13 daily food offerings were discontinued; only morning and evening incense and candles were burned.

sentences.zh: 十五年，罷冊封大饗，遣官祗告後殿。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, the great offering at investiture was discontinued; officials were dispatched to announce respectfully in the rear hall.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 the investiture great offering was discontinued; officials were sent to announce respectfully in the rear hall.

sentences.zh: 凡上徽號、冊立、御經筵、耕耤、謁陵、巡狩、迴鑾亦如之。

translations.literal: The same applied to bestowing honorific titles, investiture of an empress, attending the classics lecture, plowing the sacred field, visiting the tombs, imperial tours, and return of the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The same applied to bestowing honorific titles, investiture of an empress, the classics lecture, plowing the sacred field, tomb visits, imperial tours, and the return of the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，准太廟時饗例，增上香儀。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, following the seasonal offering precedent of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the incense-offering rite was added.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 13, following the Imperial Ancestral Temple seasonal-offering precedent, an incense rite was added.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年修殿，徙神位暫安太廟。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong the hall was repaired and the spirit seats were temporarily installed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 2 the hall was repaired and the spirit seats were temporarily placed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 其秋會值太祖、太宗忌辰，帝擬親饗，群臣言故事無素服入廟，乃止。

translations.literal: That autumn the assembly coincided with the death anniversaries of Taizu and Taizong; the emperor planned to sacrifice in person, but the ministers said precedent had no entering the temple in plain mourning garb, and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn coincided with Taizu and Taizong's death anniversaries; the emperor intended to sacrifice in person, but ministers noted that precedent allowed no plain mourning in the temple, and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，增修後殿龕座。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang the rear-hall shrines and seats were enlarged and repaired.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 1 the rear-hall shrines and seats were enlarged and repaired.

sentences.zh: 中室列龕三，奉太祖、太宗、世祖。

translations.literal: The central chamber had three shrines, enshrining Taizu, Taizong, and Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: The central chamber held three shrines for Taizu, Taizong, and Shizu.

sentences.zh: 左一室龕二，奉聖祖、高宗。

translations.literal: The left chamber had two shrines, enshrining the Sacred Ancestor and Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: The left chamber had two shrines for the Sacred Ancestor and Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 右一室龕二，奉世宗、仁宗。

translations.literal: The right chamber had two shrines, enshrining Shizong and Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: The right chamber had two shrines for Shizong and Renzong.

sentences.zh: 昭、穆仍舊制。

translations.literal: Zhao and Mu still followed the old regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The zhao and mu arrangement still followed the old regulation.

sentences.zh: 餘四室分列八龕焉。

translations.literal: The remaining four chambers were divided into eight shrines.
translations.idiomatic: The other four chambers were divided into eight shrines.

sentences.zh: 凡親饗，先三日致齋。

translations.literal: For all personal great offerings, three days beforehand fasting was observed.
translations.idiomatic: For every personal great offering, three days of fasting were observed beforehand.

sentences.zh: 先一日，掌儀司進祝版，割牲瘞毛血，潔治祭品。

translations.literal: One day beforehand the Directorate of Ceremonial presented the invocation board, slaughtered the victim and buried the hair and blood, and purified the sacrificial goods.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve, the Directorate of Ceremonial presented the invocation board, slaughtered the victim and buried hair and blood, and prepared the offerings.

sentences.zh: 屆日昧爽，內監啟寢室神龕，執事官各事咸備。

translations.literal: On the day, at dawn, eunuchs opened the sleeping-chamber spirit shrines and all officiants had their duties ready.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the day, eunuchs opened the sleeping-chamber shrines and all officiants stood ready.

sentences.zh: 內府官省畢，分詣寢室前，跪上香，三叩，興。

translations.literal: When the inner-palace officers had inspected, they went separately before the sleeping chamber, knelt, offered incense, three kowtows, and rose.
translations.idiomatic: After inner-palace officers had inspected, they went before the sleeping chamber, knelt, offered incense, kowtowed three times, and rose.

sentences.zh: 奉列聖、列後神位以次行。

translations.literal: The spirit seats of the successive sages and consorts were carried forth in order.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit seats of successive emperors and empresses were carried forth in order.

sentences.zh: 皇后祔饗，同至前殿，安於座位，南鄉，祔後西鄉。

translations.literal: When an empress was enshrined in joint offering, they went together to the front hall, installed at the seats—facing south for the enshrined consort, facing west for the consort enshrined afterward.
translations.idiomatic: When an empress was enshrined for joint offering, they went together to the front hall; the enshrined consort faced south, the later-enshrined consort faced west.

sentences.zh: 詣各香案前跪，三叩，興。

translations.literal: They went before each incense table, knelt, three kowtows, and rose.
translations.idiomatic: They knelt before each incense table, kowtowed three times, and rose.

sentences.zh: 屆時帝袞服出宮，至誠肅門降輿，入左門，盥訖，就拜位，北面立，迓神，奏貽平章。

translations.literal: At the hour the emperor in mourning dress left the palace, descended from the palanquin at the Gate of Sincere Reverence, entered the left gate, finished washing, took his obeisance place, stood facing north, welcomed the spirits, and the music "Yi Ping Zhang" was played.
translations.idiomatic: At the appointed hour the emperor in mourning dress left the palace, descended at the Gate of Sincere Reverence, entered the left gate, washed, took his obeisance place facing north, welcomed the spirits, and "Yi Ping Zhang" was played.

sentences.zh: 導詣太祖香案前，跪上炷香一，瓣香三。

translations.literal: Led to Taizu's incense table, he knelt and offered one stick of incense and three pinches of loose incense.
translations.idiomatic: He was led to Taizu's incense table, knelt, and offered one stick and three pinches of incense.

sentences.zh: 旋位，行三跪九叩禮。

translations.literal: He returned to his place and performed the three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to his place and performed three kneelings and nine prostrations.

sentences.zh: 導詣皇后香案前，立上香，旋位。

translations.literal: Led to the empress's incense table, he stood and offered incense, then returned to his place.
translations.idiomatic: He was led to the empress's incense table, stood to offer incense, and returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 行初獻禮，奏敉平章，舞干戚，有司揭尊冪，勺挹實爵，司帛、司爵以次至各案前。

translations.literal: The initial offering rite was performed; "Shu Ping Zhang" was played and shield-and-axe dance performed; officials removed the vessel covers, ladled and filled the goblets, and the silk and goblet officers in turn came before each table.
translations.idiomatic: For the initial offering, "Shu Ping Zhang" was played and the shield-and-axe dance performed; covers were removed, goblets filled, and silk and goblet officers came before each table in turn.

sentences.zh: 獻訖，司祝詣祝案前跪，三叩，興。

translations.literal: When the offering was finished, the prayer officer went before the invocation table, knelt, three kowtows, and rose.
translations.idiomatic: When the offering was finished, the prayer officer knelt before the invocation table, kowtowed three times, and rose.

sentences.zh: 跪案左，奉祝版。

translations.literal: He knelt to the left of the table and held the invocation board.
translations.idiomatic: Kneeling left of the table, he held the invocation board.

sentences.zh: 帝跪，司祝讀祝，興，安於篚，叩如初。

translations.literal: The emperor knelt; the prayer officer read the invocation, rose, placed it in the basket, and kowtowed as at first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knelt; the prayer officer read the invocation, rose, placed the board in the basket, and kowtowed as before.

sentences.zh: 帝三叩，興。

translations.literal: The emperor kowtowed three times and rose.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kowtowed three times and rose.

sentences.zh: 行亞獻禮，奏敷平章，舞羽籥，獻爵，儀如初。

translations.literal: The secondary offering rite was performed; "Fu Ping Zhang" was played and feather-and reed dance performed; goblets were offered, the rite as at the initial offering.
translations.idiomatic: The secondary offering was performed to "Fu Ping Zhang" with feather-and-reed dance; goblets were offered as at the initial offering.

sentences.zh: 行終獻禮，奏紹平章，餘並同初獻。

translations.literal: The final offering rite was performed; "Shao Ping Zhang" was played; the rest was the same as the initial offering.
translations.idiomatic: The final offering was performed to "Shao Ping Zhang"; the rest matched the initial offering.

sentences.zh: 徹饌，奏光平章。

translations.literal: The feast was withdrawn; "Guang Ping Zhang" was played.
translations.idiomatic: The offerings were withdrawn to "Guang Ping Zhang."

sentences.zh: 畢，請神還寢室，三叩，退。

translations.literal: When finished, the spirits were invited back to the sleeping chamber; three kowtows, and withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: When finished, the spirits were escorted back to the sleeping chamber; after three kowtows all withdrew.

sentences.zh: 贊「舉還宮樂」，奏乂平章，帝復行三跪九叩。

translations.literal: The master of ceremonies announced "Raise the return-to-palace music"; "Yi Ping Zhang" was played, and the emperor again performed three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies called "Raise the return-to-palace music"; "Yi Ping Zhang" was played and the emperor again performed three kneelings and nine prostrations.

sentences.zh: 司祝、司帛以次送燎所，帝轉立東旁。

translations.literal: The prayer officer and silk officer in turn sent items to the burning place; the emperor turned to stand on the east side.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer and silk officers sent offerings to the burning place in turn; the emperor stood aside to the east.

sentences.zh: 禮成，仍出左門。

translations.literal: When the rite was finished, he still went out by the left gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, he still departed by the left gate.

sentences.zh: 餘如來儀。

translations.literal: The rest followed the incoming rite.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder followed the established rite.

sentences.zh: 或遣皇子代祭，前諸儀同。

translations.literal: Sometimes a prince was sent to sacrifice in his stead; the foregoing rites were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes a prince substituted; the preceding rites were the same.

sentences.zh: 殿門外正中設拜位，入右門，至西階下盥手，升階詣拜位行禮。

translations.literal: A place for obeisance was set at the center outside the hall gate; entering the right gate, he washed his hands below the west steps, ascended, and went to the obeisance place to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: An obeisance place was set outside the central gate; entering the right gate, he washed below the west steps, ascended, and performed the rite at the obeisance place.

sentences.zh: 祝、帛送燎，避立西旁，仍自西階退。

translations.literal: The invocation and silk were sent to be burned; he stood aside to the west and still withdrew by the west steps.
translations.idiomatic: Invocation and silk were sent to the fire; he stood aside to the west and withdrew by the west steps.

sentences.zh: 其月朔薦新，正月鯉魚、青韭、鴨卵，二月萵苣、菠菜、小蔥、芹菜、鱖魚，三月王瓜、蔞萵、芸薹、茼蒿、蘿卜，四月櫻桃、茄子、雛雞，五月桃、杏、李、桑葚、蕨香、瓜子、鵝，六月杜梨、西瓜、葡萄、蘋果，七月梨、蓮子、菱、藕、榛仁、野雞，八月山藥、栗實、野鴨，九月柿、雁，十月松仁、輭棗、蘑菇、木耳，十一月銀魚、鹿肉，十二月蓼芽、綠豆芽、兔、蟫蝗魚。

translations.literal: For the first-of-month presentation of new produce: the first month—carp, green leeks, duck eggs; second month—lettuce, spinach, scallions, celery, mandarin fish; third month—cucumber, gourd, rape, crown daisy, radish; fourth month—cherry, eggplant, young chicken; fifth month—peach, apricot, plum, mulberry, bracken, melon seeds, goose; sixth month—pear, watermelon, grape, apple; seventh month—pear, lotus seed, water chestnut, lotus root, hazelnut, pheasant; eighth month—yam, chestnut, wild duck; ninth month—persimmon, wild goose; tenth month—pine nut, soft jujube, mushroom, wood ear; eleventh month—whitebait, venison; twelfth month—polygonum shoots, mung-bean sprouts, rabbit, lamprey.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly new offerings on the first: first month—carp, green leeks, duck eggs; second—lettuce, spinach, scallions, celery, mandarin fish; third—cucumber, gourd, rape, crown daisy, radish; fourth—cherry, eggplant, young chicken; fifth—peach, apricot, plum, mulberry, bracken, melon seeds, goose; sixth—pear, watermelon, grape, apple; seventh—pear, lotus seed, water chestnut, lotus root, hazelnut, pheasant; eighth—yam, chestnut, wild duck; ninth—persimmon, wild goose; tenth—pine nut, soft jujube, mushroom, wood ear; eleventh—whitebait, venison; twelfth—polygonum shoots, mung-bean sprouts, rabbit, lamprey.

sentences.zh: 其豌豆、大麥、文官果諸鮮品，或廷旨特薦者，隨時內監獻之。

translations.literal: Peas, barley, and civil-official fruit and other fresh items, or whatever the court especially ordered presented, were offered at the proper time by inner eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Peas, barley, civil-official fruit, and other fresh items—or whatever the court specially ordered—were offered in season by inner eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 順治十四年，定月薦鮮獻粢盛牲品。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Shunzhi it was fixed that monthly presentation of fresh produce should include grain offerings and sacrificial victims.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 14 monthly fresh offerings were fixed to include grain offerings and sacrificial victims.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，定薦新日，掌儀司詣後殿行禮。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi the day of new presentation was fixed; the Directorate of Ceremonial went to the rear hall to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13 the new-offering day was fixed and the Directorate of Ceremonial performed the rite in the rear hall.

sentences.zh: 獻帛爵用侍衛。

translations.literal: Presentation of silk and goblets employed bodyguards.
translations.idiomatic: Bodyguards presented the silk and goblets.

sentences.zh: 壽皇殿舊制三室，在景山東北。

translations.literal: The old regulation for the Hall of Imperial Longevity was three chambers, northeast of Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Imperial Longevity originally had three chambers northeast of Jingshan.

sentences.zh: 太祖、太宗、世祖及列後聖容，向奉體仁閣。

translations.literal: The imperial portraits of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu, and the successive consorts had formerly been kept in the Hall of Cherishing Humanity.
translations.idiomatic: Portraits of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu, and successive empresses had long been kept in the Hall of Cherishing Humanity.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，命御史莽鵠立繪聖祖御容，供奉壽皇殿中殿，遇聖誕、忌辰、元旦、令節，率皇子、近支王公展謁奠獻。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, the censor Mang Hu was ordered to paint the Sacred Ancestor's portrait and install it in the central chamber of the Hall of Imperial Longevity; on birthdays, death anniversaries, New Year's Day, and statutory festivals, princes and close-branch princes were led to pay respects and offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 the censor Mang Hu was ordered to paint the Sacred Ancestor's portrait for the central chamber of the Hall of Imperial Longevity; on birthdays, death anniversaries, New Year's Day, and statutory festivals, princes and close kin were led to pay respects and offer sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 凡奉安山陵、升祔太廟禮成，皆親詣致祭。

translations.literal: Whenever installation at the mountain tomb or enshrinement in the Imperial Ancestral Temple was finished, the emperor always went in person to sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever burial at the imperial tomb or enshrinement in the Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed, the emperor went in person to sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 蓋月必瞻禮，或至三詣焉。

translations.literal: Thus every month he would pay respects, sometimes going as many as three times.
translations.idiomatic: He paid respects every month, sometimes as often as three times.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，奉世宗聖容東一室，嗣後列朝聖容，依次奉東西室，為恆例。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong the Sacred Ancestor's portrait was installed in the east chamber; thereafter successive imperial portraits were installed in the east and west chambers in order, as a constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 the Sacred Ancestor's portrait was placed in the east chamber; thereafter each reign's portrait was installed in the east and west chambers in order as constant practice.

sentences.zh: 三年，定謁陵、省方啟蹕、迴鑾均詣壽皇殿行禮。

translations.literal: In the third year it was fixed that visiting the tombs, setting out on provincial tour, and return of the imperial carriage should all include rites at the Hall of Imperial Longevity.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 tomb visits, setting out on tour, and the return of the carriage were all fixed to include rites at the Hall of Imperial Longevity.

sentences.zh: 尋定萬壽節行禮如諸令節儀。

translations.literal: Soon the Longevity Day rite was fixed to follow the rites of other statutory festivals.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Longevity Day observances were fixed to follow other statutory festival rites.

sentences.zh: 十三年，徙建景山正中，如安佑宮制。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year it was moved and rebuilt at the center of Jingshan, on the model of the Palace of Tranquil Succor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 it was rebuilt at the center of Jingshan, following the Palace of Tranquil Succor model.

sentences.zh: 大殿九室，左右殿各三楹，東西配殿各五楹，其冬成。

translations.literal: The great hall had nine chambers; the left and right halls each three bays; the east and west side halls each five bays—it was completed that winter.
translations.idiomatic: The main hall had nine chambers, flanking halls of three bays each, and east and west side halls of five bays each; it was completed that winter.

sentences.zh: 高宗親制碑記，其頌曰：「唯堯巍巍，唯舜重華，祖考則之。

translations.literal: Gaozong personally composed the stele inscription; its eulogy says: "Only Yao was lofty, only Shun was glorious; ancestors and fathers took them as models.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong composed the stele inscription himself; the eulogy begins: "Only Yao was lofty, only Shun was glorious; ancestors and fathers took them as models.

sentences.zh: 不競不絿，仁漸義摩，祖考式之。

translations.literal: Without contention, without excess, benevolence spreading and righteousness polishing—ancestors and fathers patterned themselves on this.
translations.idiomatic: Without contention or excess, with benevolence spreading and righteousness polishing—ancestors and fathers patterned themselves on this.

sentences.zh: 弘仁皇仁，明憲帝憲，小子職之。

translations.literal: Expansive benevolence, august benevolence, enlightened statutes and imperial statutes—the young ruler performs his duty.
translations.idiomatic: Expansive benevolence, august benevolence, enlightened statutes and imperial statutes—the young ruler performs his duty.

sentences.zh: 是繼是繩，曰明曰旦，小子忽之。

translations.literal: Continuing and sustaining, bright dawn upon bright dawn—the young ruler must not neglect this.
translations.idiomatic: Continuing and sustaining, bright dawn upon bright dawn—the young ruler must not neglect it.

sentences.zh: 天游雲殂，春露秋霜，予心惻惻。

translations.literal: Heaven roams, clouds perish; spring dew and autumn frost—the heart is deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven roams, clouds perish; spring dew and autumn frost—my heart is deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 考奉祖御，於是壽皇，予仍即之。

translations.literal: The father enshrines the grandfather's portrait—here at the Hall of Imperial Longevity I still draw near.
translations.idiomatic: The father enshrines the grandfather's portrait—here at the Hall of Imperial Longevity I still draw near.

sentences.zh: 制廣而正，爰經爰營，工勿亟之。

translations.literal: The plan broad and correct, measuring and building—workers, do not hurry.
translations.idiomatic: The plan broad and correct, measuring and building—workers, do not hurry.

sentences.zh: 陟降依憑，居歆攸室，羹牆得之。

translations.literal: Ascending and descending in reliance, dwelling where spirits enjoy—the soup-on-the-wall is attained.
translations.idiomatic: Ascending and descending in reliance, where spirits dwell and enjoy—the vision on the wall is attained.

sentences.zh: 佑我後嗣，綿於萬，匪萬億之。

translations.literal: Aid my later descendants, extending for ten thousand—not ten thousand hundred-millions.
translations.idiomatic: Aid my later descendants, extending for ten thousand—not ten thousand hundred-millions.

sentences.zh: 觀德於茲，無然畔援，承欽識之。」

translations.literal: Observe virtue here; do not turn aside in rebellion—receive this with reverent knowledge."
translations.idiomatic: Observe virtue here; do not turn aside in rebellion—receive this with reverent knowledge."

sentences.zh: 十五年，諭：「前代安奉神御，率在寺中，別殿淨宇，本無定所。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year an edict said: "Former dynasties enshrined imperial portraits mostly in temples, in separate halls and pure dwellings, with no fixed place.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 an edict said: "Former dynasties enshrined imperial portraits mostly in temples, in separate halls and pure dwellings, with no fixed place.

sentences.zh: 敬念列祖創垂，顯承斯在。

translations.literal: Reverently considering how the successive ancestors founded and handed down, their manifest presence lies here.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently considering how successive ancestors founded and handed down, their manifest presence lies here.

sentences.zh: 永懷先澤，瞻仰長新。

translations.literal: Ever cherishing the former bounty, gazing up is ever renewed.
translations.idiomatic: Ever cherishing the former bounty, to gaze up is ever renewed.

sentences.zh: 式衷廟祫之儀，斯協家庭之制。

translations.literal: Thus temple-and-shrine rites harmonize with household regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus temple-and-shrine rites harmonize with household regulation.

sentences.zh: 應迎列祖、列後聖容奉壽皇殿，歲朝合請懸供，肅將祼獻。」

translations.literal: The imperial portraits of the successive ancestors and consorts should be welcomed to the Hall of Imperial Longevity; at the year's audience they should be hung together for offering, and the unvested offering reverently performed."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial portraits of successive ancestors and consorts should be welcomed to the Hall of Imperial Longevity; at the year's audience they should be hung for offering and the unvested offering reverently performed."

sentences.zh: 於是奉聖祖、世宗御容，並自體仁閣迎太祖、太宗、世祖御容，乃定除夕敬懸，供鮮果、肉醬。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Sacred Ancestor's and Shizong's portraits were installed, and from the Hall of Cherishing Humanity the portraits of Taizu, Taizong, and Shizu were welcomed; then it was fixed that on New Year's Eve they were reverently hung, with fresh fruit and meat sauce offered.
translations.idiomatic: The Sacred Ancestor's and Shizong's portraits were installed, and Taizu, Taizong, and Shizu's portraits were welcomed from the Hall of Cherishing Humanity; New Year's Eve hanging was fixed, with fresh fruit and meat sauce offered.

sentences.zh: 元旦大饗，獻磁器籩豆供品，並上香行禮。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day a great offering was performed; porcelain baskets and platters of offerings were presented, and incense was offered with obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day a great offering was performed; porcelain baskets and platters were presented, with incense and obeisance.

sentences.zh: 初二日如除夕供。

translations.literal: The second day was offered as on New Year's Eve.
translations.idiomatic: The second day followed New Year's Eve offerings.

sentences.zh: 禮畢尊藏。

translations.literal: When the rite was finished they were reverently stored away.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished the portraits were reverently stored away.

sentences.zh: 又元旦帝有事堂子、奉先殿，訖，詣壽皇殿行禮。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day, when the emperor had business at the Tangzi and Hall of Ancestors, afterward he went to the Hall of Imperial Longevity to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day, after business at the Tangzi and Hall of Ancestors, the emperor went to the Hall of Imperial Longevity to perform the rite.

sentences.zh: 除夕、初二日，命皇子番行。

translations.literal: On New Year's Eve and the second day, princes took turns by roster.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Eve and the second day, princes served in rotation.

sentences.zh: 上元節供餅餌，秋季展聖容，宮殿監敬謹將事。

translations.literal: On the Lantern Festival cakes were offered; in autumn the imperial portraits were displayed, and the palace director reverently managed affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the Lantern Festival cakes were offered; in autumn imperial portraits were displayed, and the palace director managed affairs with care.

sentences.zh: 是歲繪列朝聖容成，親詣奉安，行大饗。

translations.literal: That year, when the portraits of successive reigns were finished, the emperor went in person to install them and performed the great offering.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when successive reigns' portraits were completed, the emperor installed them in person and performed the great offering.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，詔壽皇殿供奉神御，始自聖祖，凡遇忌辰、誕辰，皆應躬親展敬，示子孫遵行，安佑宮亦如之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing an edict said that imperial portraits enshrined in the Hall of Imperial Longevity began with the Sacred Ancestor; on death and birth anniversaries the emperor should personally show respect, for descendants to follow; the Palace of Tranquil Succor was the same.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4 an edict held that portraits in the Hall of Imperial Longevity began with the Sacred Ancestor; on death and birth anniversaries the emperor should personally show respect for descendants to follow; the Palace of Tranquil Succor was the same.

sentences.zh: 安佑宮在圓明園西北隅，建工始乾隆五年，迄八年蕆事。

translations.literal: The Palace of Tranquil Succor was in the northwest corner of the Old Summer Palace; construction began in the fifth year of Qianlong and was completed in the eighth.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace of Tranquil Succor stood in the Old Summer Palace's northwest corner; building began in Qianlong 5 and finished in year 8.

sentences.zh: 大殿九室，硃扉黃甍，如寢廟制。

translations.literal: The great hall had nine chambers, vermilion doors and yellow tiles, like a sleeping temple.
translations.idiomatic: The main hall had nine chambers with vermilion doors and yellow tiles, like a sleeping temple.

sentences.zh: 中龕懸聖祖御容，左世宗，右高宗。

translations.literal: The central shrine hung the Sacred Ancestor's portrait; to the left Shizong, to the right Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: The central shrine held the Sacred Ancestor's portrait, with Shizong on the left and Gaozong on the right.

sentences.zh: 龕前陳彝器、書冊、佩用服物，合設中和韶樂一列。

translations.literal: Before the shrines were set ritual vessels, books, and garments worn on the person, together with a full set of the harmonious elegant music.
translations.idiomatic: Before the shrines stood ritual vessels, books, and personal garments, with a full set of harmonious elegant music.

sentences.zh: 帝臨御園中，遇列聖誕辰，忌辰，令節，朔、望，並拈香行禮。

translations.literal: When the emperor resided in the garden, on successive sages' birthdays and death anniversaries, statutory festivals, and the first and full moon, he burned incense and performed the rite.
translations.idiomatic: While residing in the garden, on successive emperors' birthdays and death anniversaries, statutory festivals, and new and full moon, the emperor burned incense and performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 謁陵、省方啟鑾、回蹕，皆躬詣祗告焉。

translations.literal: Visiting the tombs, setting out on provincial tour, and return of the carriage—all were occasions when he went in person to announce respectfully.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb visits, setting out on tour, and return of the carriage—all were occasions for personal respectful announcement.

sentences.zh: 高宗親制碑記，略言：「朔酌望獻，西漢原廟遺制。

translations.literal: Gaozong personally composed the stele inscription, saying in brief: "Offering on the first and full moon—this is the legacy of the Former Han original temple.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong composed the stele inscription, noting in brief: "Offering on new and full moon—this follows the Former Han original temple.

sentences.zh: 宋時神御殿亦本斯義，蓋奉安列朝御容所也。

translations.literal: In Song times the spirit-portrait hall also arose from this meaning—it is where successive imperial portraits are installed.
translations.idiomatic: The Song spirit-portrait hall arose from the same idea—it is where successive imperial portraits are installed.

sentences.zh: 上元結鐙樓，寒食設鞦韆，視漢已備。

translations.literal: On First Full Moon a lantern tower was set up; on Cold Food a swing was set up—already complete compared with Han.
translations.idiomatic: On First Full Moon a lantern tower was erected; on Cold Food a swing was set up—already complete compared with Han.

sentences.zh: 而崇建遍郡國，奉祀在禪院，識者譏之。

translations.literal: Yet when construction spread through every commandery and district and worship was in Chan monasteries, critics ridiculed it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when construction spread through every commandery and worship was held in Chan monasteries, critics ridiculed it.

sentences.zh: 我皇祖聖祖，恩澤旁覃，僻邑窮谷，飲其德而不知，子孫臣庶，躬被教育者，宜其謳歌慨慕而未有已也。

translations.literal: Our august ancestor the Sacred Ancestor, whose favor spread even to remote valleys where people drank his virtue unknowingly—descendants and subjects who received his teaching in person should sing and mourn him without end.
translations.idiomatic: Our Sacred Ancestor spread favor even to remote valleys where people drank his virtue unknowingly—descendants and subjects who received his teaching should sing and mourn him without end.

sentences.zh: 是以皇考世宗謹就壽皇殿奉安御容，朔望瞻禮，而於皇祖所幸暢春園，亦陳薦如儀。

translations.literal: Therefore my august father Shizong reverently installed the portrait at the Hall of Imperial Longevity and paid respects on new and full moon; at the Ever-Spring Garden beloved of the august grandfather, offerings were also set out as in the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore my father Shizong reverently installed the portrait at the Hall of Imperial Longevity with new- and full-moon respects; at the Ever-Spring Garden beloved of the grandfather, offerings were set out as in the rite.

sentences.zh: 有漢、宋備物備禮之誠，無宋代祀繁致褻之弊。

translations.literal: There was the sincerity of Han and Song in complete objects and complete rites, without the Song fault of excessive worship leading to disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: There was Han and Song sincerity in complete objects and rites, without the Song fault of excessive worship leading to disrespect.

sentences.zh: 予小子心懍紹庭，念茲圓明園為我皇考囿沼地，築室九楹，敬奉皇祖其中，奉皇考配東一室。

translations.literal: I, the young ruler, heart fearful of continuing the court, mindful that the Old Summer Palace was my august father's park and pond, built a hall of nine bays and reverently installed the august grandfather therein, with the august father paired in the east chamber.
translations.idiomatic: I, the young ruler, fearful of continuing the court, mindful that the Old Summer Palace was my father's park, built a nine-bay hall and reverently installed the grandfather therein, with my father paired in the east chamber.

sentences.zh: 所謂禮緣義起，有其舉之，莫敢廢也。」

translations.literal: This is what is called rites arising from righteousness—where there is occasion to raise them, none dare abolish them."
translations.idiomatic: This is what is called rites arising from righteousness—where there is occasion to raise them, none dare abolish them."

sentences.zh: 永佑寺在熱河避暑山莊萬樹園旁，乾隆十六年建。

translations.literal: Yongyou Temple was beside the Ten-Thousand-Trees Garden at the Rehe Mountain Resort; it was built in the sixteenth year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyou Temple stood beside the Ten-Thousand-Trees Garden at the Rehe Mountain Resort; it was built in Qianlong 16.

sentences.zh: 有樓五楹，奉聖祖、世宗、高宗御容，雲山勝地樓奉仁宗御容，陳設一如安佑宮。

translations.literal: A five-bay tower enshrined the portraits of the Sacred Ancestor, Shizong, and Gaozong; Cloud-Mountain Scenic Place tower enshrined Renzong's portrait; furnishings were as at the Palace of Tranquil Succor.
translations.idiomatic: A five-bay tower held portraits of the Sacred Ancestor, Shizong, and Gaozong; Cloud-Mountain Scenic Place held Renzong's portrait; furnishings matched the Palace of Tranquil Succor.

sentences.zh: 車駕蒞至輒懸奉，回蹕後庋藏。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage arrived they were hung for worship; after return of the carriage they were stored away.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage arrived the portraits were hung for worship; after the return they were stored away.

sentences.zh: 丹墀列高宗御制碑文，略言：「創立精藍，爰名永佑。

translations.literal: On the red terrace Gaozong's inscribed stele was set out; it says in brief: "Establishing this refined monastery, it is named Everlasting Succor.
translations.idiomatic: On the red terrace stood Gaozong's inscribed stele, which says in brief: "Establishing this refined monastery, it is named Everlasting Succor.

sentences.zh: 固不特鍾魚梵唄，足令三十六景借證聲聞；

translations.literal: It is not only that bells, fish, and Buddhist chanting suffice to let the thirty-six scenes borrow proof of the teaching;
translations.idiomatic: It is not only that bells, fish, and Buddhist chanting let the thirty-six scenes borrow proof of the teaching;

sentences.zh: 而皇祖聖日所照，千秋萬歲後，子孫臣庶，莫不永如在之思。

translations.literal: but when the august grandfather's holy sun shines, after a thousand autumns and ten thousand years descendants and subjects will all think of him as ever present.
translations.idiomatic: but when the grandfather's holy sun shines, after a thousand autumns and ten thousand years descendants and subjects will think of him as ever present.

sentences.zh: 是即釋迦之耆闍崛山，金剛法座，天龍擁護；

translations.literal: This is like Sakyamuni's Gridhrakuta, the diamond dharma seat, guarded by heavenly dragons;
translations.idiomatic: This is like Sakyamuni's Vulture Peak, the diamond dharma seat, guarded by heavenly dragons;

sentences.zh: 而所以繩武寧親，祝釐養志，亦於是託焉云爾。」

translations.literal: and thus continuing martial achievement and comforting kin, praying for blessing and nourishing filial intent, are also entrusted here."
translations.idiomatic: and thus continuing martial achievement, comforting kin, praying for blessing, and nourishing filial intent are also entrusted here."

sentences.zh: 仁宗御制永佑寺瞻禮敬紀，亦頗惓惓祖若父焉。

translations.literal: Renzong's composition commemorating worship at Yongyou Temple also dwelt earnestly on grandfather and father.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong's commemoration of worship at Yongyou Temple also dwelt earnestly on grandfather and father.

sentences.zh: 道光時，移供聖御繼德堂，更題曰綏成殿。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang period the sacred portraits were moved to the Hall of Continuing Virtue, which was retitled the Hall of Lasting Completion.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daoguang period the sacred portraits were moved to the Hall of Continuing Virtue, retitled the Hall of Lasting Completion.

sentences.zh: 中室聖祖，左世宗，右高宗，左次室仁宗，以後列朝御容，仍依次懸左右室雲。

translations.literal: The central chamber held the Sacred Ancestor; to the left Shizong, to the right Gaozong; the left secondary chamber held Renzong; thereafter successive imperial portraits were still hung in the left and right chambers in order.
translations.idiomatic: The central chamber held the Sacred Ancestor, Shizong left and Gaozong right; the left secondary chamber held Renzong; later reigns' portraits were still hung in the side chambers in order.

sentences.zh: 滿洲俗尚跳神，其儀，內室供神牌，或用木龕，室正中、西北龕各一。

translations.literal: Manchu custom favored the spirit dance; in the rite, the inner chamber supplied spirit tablets, or wooden shrines were used—one in the center of the room and one in the northwest niche.
translations.idiomatic: Manchu custom favored the spirit dance; in the rite the inner chamber supplied spirit tablets or wooden shrines—one at the room's center and one in the northwest niche.

sentences.zh: 凡室南鄉北鄉，以西方為上；

translations.literal: For all rooms facing south or north, the west was regarded as upper;
translations.idiomatic: In rooms facing south or north, the west was regarded as upper;

sentences.zh: 東鄉西鄉，以南方為上：頗與禮經合。

translations.literal: for rooms facing east or west, the south was regarded as upper—quite in accord with the ritual classics.
translations.idiomatic: in rooms facing east or west, the south was upper—quite in accord with the ritual classics.

sentences.zh: 南龕下懸簾幕，黃雲緞為之。

translations.literal: Below the southern shrine a curtain of yellow cloud brocade was hung.
translations.idiomatic: Below the southern shrine hung a curtain of yellow cloud brocade.

sentences.zh: 北龕上置杌，杌下陳香盤三，木為之。

translations.literal: Above the northern shrine a stool was placed; below it three incense trays of wood were set out.
translations.idiomatic: Above the northern shrine stood a stool; below it were three wooden incense trays.

sentences.zh: 春、秋擇日致祭，謂為跳神。

translations.literal: In spring and autumn an auspicious day was chosen for sacrifice—this was called the spirit dance.
translations.idiomatic: In spring and autumn an auspicious day was chosen for sacrifice—called the spirit dance.

sentences.zh: 前一月，造酒神房。

translations.literal: One month beforehand a spirit-wine room was built.
translations.idiomatic: One month beforehand a spirit-wine room was constructed.

sentences.zh: 前三日，朝暮獻牲各二，名曰烏雲，即引祀也。

translations.literal: Three days beforehand, morning and evening, two victims each were offered—called "leading the sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Three days beforehand, morning and evening, two victims each were offered—called "leading the sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 前一日，神前供打糕各九盤，以為散獻。

translations.literal: One day beforehand, before the spirit, nine platters of pounded cake were offered as scattered presentation.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve, nine platters of pounded cake were offered before the spirit as scattered presentation.

sentences.zh: 大祀日，五鼓獻糕，主人吉服鄉西跪，設神幄鄉東，中設如來、觀音神位。

translations.literal: On the great-sacrifice day, at the fifth watch cakes were offered; the master in auspicious dress knelt facing west; a spirit canopy facing east was set up, with Tathagata and Guanyin spirit seats in the center.
translations.idiomatic: On the great-sacrifice day, at the fifth watch cakes were offered; the master in auspicious dress knelt facing west; a spirit canopy faced east with Tathagata and Guanyin seats in the center.

sentences.zh: 女巫舞刀祝曰：「敬獻糕餌，以祈康年。」

translations.literal: The shamaness danced with a knife and prayed: "Reverently offering cakes and millet to pray for a peaceful year."
translations.idiomatic: The shamaness danced with a knife and prayed: "Reverently offering cakes and millet to pray for a peaceful year."

sentences.zh: 主人跪擊神版，諸護衛亦擊，並彈弦、箏、月琴和之，其聲嗚嗚然。

translations.literal: The master knelt and struck the spirit board; bodyguards also struck, and zither, zheng, and moon lute harmonized—the sound was a low humming.
translations.idiomatic: The master knelt and struck the spirit board; bodyguards struck too, with zither, zheng, and moon lute—the sound was a low hum.

sentences.zh: 巫歌畢，主人一叩，興。

translations.literal: When the shaman's song was finished, the master kowtowed once and rose.
translations.idiomatic: When the shaman's song ended, the master kowtowed once and rose.

sentences.zh: 司香婦請神出。

translations.literal: The incense woman requested the spirit to come forth.
translations.idiomatic: The incense woman invited the spirit forth.

sentences.zh: 戶牖西設龕，南鄉奉之。

translations.literal: A shrine was set west of the door and window, facing south to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine was set west of the door and window, facing south to receive the spirit.

sentences.zh: 司俎者呼「進牲」，牲入，主人跪，家人皆跪。

translations.literal: The meat-offering officer called "Advance the victim"; the victim entered; the master knelt and all the household knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The meat officer called "Advance the victim"; when it entered, the master knelt and the whole household knelt.

sentences.zh: 巫者前致辭，以酒灌牲耳，牲耳甡，司俎高聲曰：「神已領牲。」

translations.literal: The shaman advanced and delivered the invocation; wine was poured on the victim's ear; when the ear quivered, the meat officer cried loudly: "The spirit has received the victim."
translations.idiomatic: The shaman delivered the invocation; wine was poured on the victim's ear; when the ear quivered, the meat officer cried: "The spirit has received the victim."

sentences.zh: 主人叩謝。

translations.literal: The master kowtowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The master kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 庖人刲牲，熟而薦之。

translations.literal: The cook slaughtered the victim, cooked it, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: The cook slaughtered the victim, cooked it, and presented it.

sentences.zh: 主人再拜謁，巫致辭。

translations.literal: The master bowed twice in obeisance; the shaman delivered the invocation.
translations.idiomatic: The master bowed twice; the shaman delivered the invocation.

sentences.zh: 主人叩畢，巫以系馬吉帛進，祝如儀。

translations.literal: When the master's kowtows were finished, the shaman advanced the auspicious silk tied to the horse and prayed as in the rite.
translations.idiomatic: When the master finished kowtowing, the shaman advanced auspicious silk tied to the horse and prayed as in the rite.

sentences.zh: 主人跪領帛，以授司牧，一叩，興。

translations.literal: The master knelt to receive the silk and handed it to the herd officer; one kowtow, and rise.
translations.idiomatic: The master knelt to receive the silk, gave it to the herd officer, kowtowed once, and rose.

sentences.zh: 乃集宗人食胙肉，令毋出戶庭。

translations.literal: Then the clan assembled to eat the sacrificial flesh, with orders not to go beyond the courtyard gate.
translations.idiomatic: Then the clan assembled to eat the sacrificial flesh, forbidden to go beyond the courtyard gate.

sentences.zh: 其夕供七仙女、長白山神、遠祖、始祖，位西南鄉。

translations.literal: That evening the Seven Fairies, Changbai Mountain spirit, remote ancestors, and founding ancestor were offered, their seats facing southwest.
translations.idiomatic: That evening the Seven Fairies, Changbai Mountain spirit, remote ancestors, and founding ancestor were offered, seats facing southwest.

sentences.zh: 以神幙蔽窗牖，舞刀進牲致祝如朝儀。

translations.literal: Spirit curtains screened the windows; knife dance and advancing the victim with invocation followed the morning rite.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit curtains screened the windows; knife dance and victim presentation followed the morning rite.

sentences.zh: 唯伐銅鼓作淵淵聲，主家亦擊手鼓、架鼓，以銅鼓聲為應。

translations.literal: Only copper drums were struck with a deep booming sound; the master's household also beat hand drums and frame drums, responding to the copper-drum sound.
translations.idiomatic: Only copper drums were struck with a deep boom; the household also beat hand and frame drums in response.

sentences.zh: 誦益急，跳益甚。

translations.literal: The chanting grew urgent and the dancing more intense.
translations.idiomatic: Chanting grew urgent and dancing more intense.

sentences.zh: 禮成，眾受福。
