translations.literal: When the rite was finished, all received blessing.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished, all received blessing.

sentences.zh: 次早設位庭院前，位北鄉，主人吉服如儀。

translations.literal: Early the next morning a seat was set in the courtyard, facing north; the master in auspicious dress as in the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Next morning a seat was set in the courtyard facing north; the master wore auspicious dress as in the rite.

sentences.zh: 用男巫致辭畢，灑以米，趨退。

translations.literal: A male shaman finished the invocation, sprinkled rice, and hurried away.
translations.idiomatic: A male shaman finished the invocation, sprinkled rice, and withdrew hastily.

sentences.zh: 主人叩拜。

translations.literal: The master kowtowed in obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: The master kowtowed in obeisance.

sentences.zh: 牲肉皆刲為菹醢，和稻米以進。

translations.literal: The victim's flesh was all cut into hash and mixed with rice to present.
translations.idiomatic: All victim flesh was cut into hash, mixed with rice, and presented.

sentences.zh: 名曰祭天還原。

translations.literal: This was called "sacrifice to Heaven and return to origin."
translations.idiomatic: This was called "sacrifice to Heaven and return to origin."

sentences.zh: 又明日，神位前祈福，供餅餌，綴五色縷。

translations.literal: On the following day, before the spirit seat, prayer for blessing was offered; cakes were presented, strung with threads of five colors.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, before the spirit seat, prayer for blessing was offered with cakes strung on threads of five colors.

sentences.zh: 祝辭畢，以縷系主人胸，謂之受福。

translations.literal: When the invocation was finished, the threads were tied on the master's chest—this was called receiving blessing.
translations.idiomatic: When the invocation ended, the threads were tied on the master's chest—called receiving blessing.

sentences.zh: 三日祭乃畢。

translations.literal: On the third day the sacrifice was finished.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day the sacrifice was complete.

sentences.zh: 長白滿洲舊族近興京城者，祀典禮儀皆同。

translations.literal: Changbai Manchu old clans near the capital all had the same sacrificial rites and ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Changbai Manchu clans near the capital followed the same sacrificial rites and ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 唯舒穆祿氏供昊天上帝、如來、菩薩諸像，又供貂神其側。

translations.literal: Only the Sumuru clan offered images of the Supreme Heavenly Lord, Tathagata, Bodhisattva, and others, and also offered the sable spirit at the side.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Sumuru clan offered images of the Supreme Heavenly Lord, Tathagata, Bodhisattva, and others, and also the sable spirit at the side.

sentences.zh: 納蘭氏則供羊、雞、魚、鴨諸品，巫者身系銅鈴跳舞，以鈴墜為宜男兆。

translations.literal: The Nara clan offered sheep, chicken, fish, duck, and other items; the shaman wore copper bells on the body and danced—the falling of the bells was taken as an omen of obtaining a son.
translations.idiomatic: The Nara clan offered sheep, chicken, fish, duck, and other items; shamans danced with copper bells on the body—the bells falling was an omen of obtaining a son.

sentences.zh: 蒙古跳神用羊、酒，輝和跳神以一人介胄持弓矢坐牆堵，蓋先世有劫祀者，故豫使人防之，因沿為制。

translations.literal: Mongol spirit dance used sheep and wine; Huihe spirit dance had one man in armor with bow and arrow seated on the wall—because in former times there were raiders at the sacrifice, a man was posted in advance for defense, and this became regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol spirit dance used sheep and wine; Huihe had a man in armor with bow and arrow seated on the wall—because raiders once attacked the sacrifice, a guard was posted and the practice became regulation.

sentences.zh: 跳神之舉，清初盛行，其誦祝辭者曰薩嗎，迄嘉慶時，罕用薩嗎跳神者，然其祭固未嘗廢也。

translations.literal: The spirit dance was prevalent in the early Qing; those who chanted the invocation were called saman; by the Jiaqing period saman were rarely used for the spirit dance, yet the sacrifice was never discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit dance was prevalent in the early Qing; invocation chanters were called saman; by Jiaqing saman were rarely used, yet the sacrifice was never discontinued.
